rows.description: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. *Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.An overview of this role As an AI Transformation Owner at GitLab, you'll shape your function's AI strategy and build the solutions that deliver it. You are the person responsible for identifying where AI can fundamentally change how your org operates, partnering with your Executive Sponsor to align on the biggest challenges, and driving measurable outcomes against them. Think of this as a product management role where the product is your org's way of working. You'll manage the full lifecycle: understanding how work flows today, deciding where AI should reshape it, prioritizing what gets built and in what order, and ensuring what ships actually gets adopted. You'll also prototype solutions, configure agents, and prove what's possible before pulling in engineering support to scale it. You will work closely with an AI Engineer who sits within the Enterprise AI team. Together you form a partnership: you bring the business context, process intelligence, and strategic prioritization. They bring the technical depth, production-grade delivery, and architecture decisions. You'll build working solutions at the no-code and low-code layer, and partner with the AI Engineer on the right approach, tooling, and structure. What you'll do Strategy & Prioritization Own your function's AI strategy, aligned with your Executive Sponsor and business priorities. Understand which metrics matter to the org, identify what will move the needle, define how you'll measure impact, and track progress over time. Map how work flows across your function end-to-end, including the handoffs upstream and downstream to other orgs. Identify where the real constraints are, not just the ones your team can see. Focus on the 100x problems: where could leveraging AI in a workflow let your org execute it orders of magnitude faster, or at 100x more volume than before? Manage intake of AI requests, ideas, and pain points from across the function, including via your Champion network. Ensure every team member has a clear route to surface what they need, rather than building independently. Prioritize strategically against business outcomes and executive guidance. Hold the line on priorities - we cannot change direction every two weeks - and ensure the AI Engineer's time is spent on the highest-impact work. Adoption & Change Management Reimagine, not just automate. Challenge your org to think beyond injecting AI into existing workflows. Work with Enterprise AI to spot opportunities to fundamentally rethink how work gets done. Drive adoption and change management together with the AI Engineer. The best AI solution is worthless if nobody uses it. Create the channels, rituals, and feedback loops that make AI visible in your function: shared spaces for teams to show what they've built, regular office hours, onboarding for new hires, and celebration of wins. Own the rollout and iteration needed to make AI initiatives stick. Coordinate with Enterprise AI to ensure your function benefits from patterns, tools, and learnings emerging across other parts of the business. Build and bridge the Champion network in your function. Champions are the peer community that extends your reach beyond what you and the AI Engineer can deliver directly. From early in the role, identify and recruit Champions across sub-teams (5-10% time, formally agreed with their manager), run a regular Champion sync, host demos to the wider function, and act as their bridge to Enterprise AI. Champions are not your reports: you coordinate them, you don't manage them. Without this network, your reach is capped. Hands-On Building & Agent Operations Build AI agents using no-code and low-code platforms (e.g. Glean, Workato, similar tools). Go from idea to working prototype without waiting for engineering. Author and iterate on skills files that define how AI agents behave. Refine instructions based on real usage and share reusable skills across the function. Configure MCP servers and tools, giving agents access to the business systems they need. Partner with the AI Engineer on what to connect and how to do it securely. Own your function's fleet of agents. Some agents will be used directly by people in your org. Those that aren't, you own. Either way, you're accountable for their performance: tracking KPIs, running evaluations after model or data changes, and iterating based on what you learn. Expect to rebuild. AI tools and models evolve fast. The agent you built last month may need to be replaced, not patched. You should be comfortable sunsetting your own work when a better approach emerges, and helping your org stay current rather than attached to what exists today. What you'll bring Business & Strategic Deep knowledge of your function's operations. You understand how work moves through your org, where it gets stuck, and why. You can trace a process end-to-end and explain how it connects to the teams around it. Strategic prioritization skills. You've managed competing demands before and can make hard calls about what matters most. You think in terms of business outcomes, not activity. A product management mindset. You naturally think about intake, backlog, iteration, and adoption. You're comfortable defining success metrics and holding yourself accountable to them. Strong communication and influence. You'll be the person saying "not yet" to some teams and "think bigger" to others. You need the credibility and interpersonal skills to make both of those conversations land. Cross-functional instincts. You default to understanding how your org's processes affect and are affected by the teams around you - not just optimising in isolation. Experience building peer networks or communities of practice. You've recruited and sustained volunteer contributors before, whether as a guild lead, champion program owner, or community organizer. You know how to motivate people whose time you don't directly own. Hands-On & Technical Comfortable building with AI tools. You don't need to write production code, but you should be able to build a working agent, configure a skill, connect an MCP server, and troubleshoot when something isn't working. Think: power user, not software engineer. Ready to learn fast. Experience with or willingness to quickly pick up no-code/low-code AI platforms, prompt engineering, and agent configuration. You'll be trained on GitLab's specific tooling, but you should arrive ready to get your hands dirty. Strong conceptual understanding of AI capabilities - summarization, classification, generation, automation, agentic workflows - and a commitment to staying current. The landscape shifts constantly. The tools you use today may be obsolete in weeks. You stay on top of new developments so that your org's AI strategy reflects what's actually possible, not what was possible six months ago. Ability to map data flows - structured and unstructured. Understand where agents need context, and figure out where humans should interface with automated workflows and at what steps. About the team You will partner closely with Enterprise AI within the Enterprise Technology & AI organization, while remaining embedded in your own function. Enterprise AI provides the technical delivery capability, platforms, and patterns. You provide the business context, prioritization, building at the no-code layer, and adoption muscle. rows.role: Principal Product Manager - Core Experience Platform
rows.description:
We design Spotify’s consumer experience—end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints—from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify.
The Core Experience team builds the foundations that make Spotify feel connected, intuitive, and consistent wherever people listen. From Playlists to shared product capabilities, we help teams across Spotify create experiences that millions of listeners use every day.
We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to shape the future of these platforms. You'll set product direction, bring teams together around shared priorities, and help create the capabilities that make great listening experiences possible at scale. This is an opportunity to influence how Spotify's products evolve while making a meaningful impact on listeners and creators around the world.

What You’ll Do:
Partner with engineering leaders to explore technical solutions, evaluate trade-offs, and guide decisions that improve product performance, reliability, and scalability. Develop shared platform capabilities that help teams build consistent, high-quality experiences across Spotify. Improve the adoption and long-term value of platform capabilities by gathering feedback, measuring outcomes, and supporting teams that use them. Balance new product opportunities with technical improvements, including system performance, quality, simplification, and platform migrations. Use experimentation, prototypes, technical exploration, and feedback to test ideas, learn quickly, and adapt your approach. Build alignment across teams by communicating priorities, dependencies, and trade-offs clearly, helping partners work toward shared outcomes.

Who You Are:
You have 5+ years of product management experience, including experience building or improving technical platforms, shared systems, or capabilities that support consumer products. You understand client and backend technologies and can work with engineers to connect technical decisions to user needs and business outcomes. You're familiar with mobile development for iOS or Android, including areas such as app performance, reliability, user interface architecture, or design systems. You have experience guiding products or platforms beyond launch, improving adoption, managing technical debt, and supporting systems as needs evolve. You can evaluate technical trade-offs and make thoughtful decisions about when to improve existing systems, simplify solutions, or invest in new capabilities. You use data, research, experimentation, and sound judgment to make product decisions, including when traditional A/B testing isn't the right approach. You communicate complex ideas clearly, welcome different perspectives, and build strong relationships across engineering, design, and data teams. You're comfortable navigating ambiguity, taking ownership of complex challenges, and adapting your approach as you learn.

Where You’ll Be:
This role is based in Stockholm or London. We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.
 
At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

rows.description: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. *Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.An overview of this role As a Fullstack Engineer on the Duo Client SDK team at GitLab, you'll build the shared foundation for every GitLab Duo client. Today, the logic that powers Duo in editors lives inside the GitLab Language Server. We're extracting it into a true software development kit (SDK): a set of well-versioned TypeScript packages that editor extensions, our web-based Duo Chat on GitLab.com, and eventually external applications can use. You'll work in TypeScript across frontend and backend systems. You'll design the SDK's Node.js core and public application programming interface (API), and work in the clients that use it. The work rewards care about interfaces, versioning, and backward compatibility as much as features because other engineers will depend on what you build. You'll have senior and staff engineers alongside you to help with design. You'll own the implementation of scoped packages and ship improvements with minimal guidance while collaborating with the team on larger architectural changes. Some examples of our projects: The Duo Client SDK, extracting versioned, publishable packages from the GitLab Language Server The GitLab Language Server, rebuilt on top of the SDK as our polyglot surface Duo Chat on the web, as one of the SDK's first consumers What you'll do Develop secure, well-tested, and performant TypeScript features that solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity. Ship small features and improvements with minimal guidance, writing tests with every merge request and contributing to code reviews and design discussions. Extract and publish TypeScript packages from the GitLab Language Server, migrating consumers incrementally so no parallel implementation is left to drift. Design durable public APIs with clear interfaces, semantic versioning, changelogs, and deprecation paths for external consumers. Build isomorphic core packages that isolate platform-specific behavior in adapters at the edges. Build and improve SDK client surfaces, including Vue 3 components in Duo Chat on the web, in collaboration with product, design, and engineering teams. Strengthen credential handling across hosts, including bearer tokens, session cookies, and CSRF protection. Optimize bundle size, startup cost, and dependency weight for browser consumers, and support a Tier 2 on-call rotation for urgent engineering issues. What you'll bring Strong proficiency with TypeScript across frontend and backend systems, including experience building and maintaining Node.js services. Experience with modern build and packaging tools, including monorepos, multi-module builds, ECMAScript modules (ESM), and dependency management. Experience with Vue 3 and the Composition API, or comparable component-based frontend experience and a willingness to learn Vue. Experience designing APIs that other people use, with the ability to explain what you'd do differently. Understanding of the differences between running code in Node.js and in the browser, and how to write code that works in both. A security-minded development approach, including careful credential handling and performance optimization. Ability to communicate clearly and concisely in writing about technical problems, propose iterative solutions, and work effectively in an agile environment. Self-motivation, strong organizational skills, and the judgment to ask for help when needed while thriving in a fully remote organization aligned with GitLab's values. We collaborate across client surfaces to make thoughtful technical decisions as the platform evolves. We work fully remotely and asynchronously across regions, in the open, following GitLab's values of transparency and open communication. rows.role: Senior Digital Learning Experience Designer, Learning & Inclusion
rows.description:
We’re looking for a Senior Digital Learning Experience Designer to join our Learning & Inclusion team, the group responsible for creating learning experiences that help every Spotify band member grow, belong, and do their best work.
You’ll bring together instructional design, visual design, storytelling, and broader learning and development expertise to create inclusive and effective experiences at scale. You’ll partner with subject-matter experts, people leaders, and Learning & Inclusion colleagues on company-wide initiatives, from leadership development to programs that bring Spotify’s values to life.

What You'll Do:
Lead the end-to-end design of learning experiences, from needs analysis and curriculum architecture through development, launch, and evaluation. Partner with subject-matter experts and stakeholders to identify performance needs and turn them into clear learning objectives and practical solutions. Design learning journeys across live, digital, blended, and self-directed formats using evidence-based learning principles. Create engaging learning materials, including eLearning, facilitator guides, participant resources, job aids, presentations, and micro-learning experiences. Use visual design and storytelling to make complex ideas clear, memorable, and engaging while creating experiences that feel unmistakably Spotify. Build interactive digital learning experiences using AI-assisted workflows and authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline or Rise, Adobe Captivate, or similar platforms. Design inclusive learning experiences that reflect different perspectives, reduce barriers to participation, and support a culture of belonging. Pilot and iterate on learning experiences using learner feedback, stakeholder input, and performance data. Define meaningful measures of success and evaluate learning effectiveness, knowledge transfer, learner experience, and behavior change. Manage multiple learning projects from initial scoping through delivery while creating clarity around priorities, timelines, and stakeholder expectations. Explore emerging approaches in learning design, including AI-assisted authoring and adaptive learning, and apply them where they can meaningfully improve the learner experience.

Who You Are:
You have 5+ years of professional instructional design experience and a portfolio demonstrating thoughtful work across multiple learning formats. You apply learning science principles such as cognitive load, retrieval practice, spaced learning, and adult learning theory to practical design decisions. You know how to uncover learning and performance needs, translate them into measurable objectives, and design learning journeys that build knowledge and skills over time. You create meaningful practice through scenarios, simulations, assessments, and other interactive experiences rather than relying on passive content. You have strong visual and UX design judgment and understand how typography, hierarchy, layout, and visual storytelling can make learning clearer and easier to navigate. You have experience with rapid authoring tools such as Articulate 360, Captivate, Lectora, or similar platforms, along with design tools such as Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, or equivalent. You can create clear storyboards, scripts, facilitator guides, and supporting materials that help others confidently deliver consistent learning experiences. You use learner feedback and data to evaluate effectiveness, iterate on your work, and connect learning experiences to meaningful outcomes. You communicate complex ideas clearly and collaborate effectively with subject-matter experts, leaders, and cross-functional partners. You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity, balancing multiple priorities, and taking ownership from an early idea through a polished learning experience. You bring experience in areas such as inclusive learning design, leadership development, learning technology, short-form learning video or animation, LMS/LXP platforms, or SCORM/xAPI. You have a degree in instructional design, learning sciences, education, human-computer interaction, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in London or Stockholm We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

We are looking for a strategic-minded, execution-oriented Artist & Label Partnerships Manager for France, to join Spotify’s Music team based in Paris. In this role, you will sit at the heart of the music ecosystem, moving between high-level release strategies and the day-to-day tactical execution that drives artist and business growth. This role is perfect for a music industry professional who thrives on building relationships and navigating the intersection of technology and creativity.
 
Our ideal candidate has fun at work and a desire to make a positive impact on the music industry as a whole. Above all, your work will impact the way the world experiences music and strengthen Spotify’s role as a trusted, culturally relevant voice in the music landscape.

What You'll do:
  Focusing on the French music landscape, you will be the primary point of contact for local music partners based in France, ensuring that Spotify remains the most valued partner for artists and our industry partners, utilising on-platform promotion and off-platform initiatives to ensure Spotify is the premiere platform for artist development Support and educate our key partners across artists and labels communities in France on Spotify tools, resources and insights to encourage them and improve their daily business You will contribute your expertise to various music-related projects within the company, executing on creative and cross-functional collaborations in the region and beyond, building impactful and innovative artist partnerships to enable artists development and artist-fan engagement You will proactively identify music trends, emerging talent and opportunities in the local and global music landscape, providing deep cultural and musical insights with the local FR team to execute pivotal initiatives, multi-market campaigns and other key internal partners & teams including editorial, consumer marketing, communications, strategy & operations… Lead artist & label partnerships representation in high-impact cross-functional projects and strategic bets Ensure Spotify has the best possible content offering in France and use this to further Spotify's appeal to existing and new users Connect other Spotify teams with the music industry to help drive and execute opportunities driven by Spotify and our partners. rows.description:
We’re looking for a Senior C++/iOS Engineer to join the Baldur squad within User Platform (UP). Baldur owns Spotify’s Session Management and Delegated Authorization domains—the systems that enable applications to securely obtain, use, and manage access tokens for hundreds of millions of users. In this role, you’ll help shape the technology that powers secure access across every Spotify client and third-party integration. 
Your work will support engineers across Spotify building mobile and desktop experiences, platform teams, and third-party developers integrating with Spotify’s authorization platform. You’ll collaborate across disciplines to build secure, reliable, and scalable authentication experiences that have a direct impact on millions of people every day.

What You'll Do:
Collaborate with a highly autonomous and supportive engineering squad responsible for Spotify’s delegated authorization and session management platforms. Design, build, and evolve critical infrastructure powering Spotify applications and partner integrations using shared C++ libraries and native Swift on iOS. Develop secure, reliable, and performant delegated authorization flows, including token issuance, refresh, revocation, and session lifecycle management across multiple platforms. Partner with client and backend engineers to integrate with core authorization services, token issuance, client registration, and token revocation. Improve how credentials and access tokens are securely stored and managed on-device while balancing security, reliability, and application performance. Contribute to the evolution of Spotify’s authorization frameworks, Spotify-specific implementations, enabling new platforms and product experiences. Drive technical improvements, share knowledge with teammates, and help shape the long-term technical direction of delegated authorization and session management.

Who You Are:
You have strong proficiency in C++, along with experience building native iOS applications in Swift, or you're excited to develop your expertise in Swift while applying your C++ skills. You have experience designing, building, or maintaining security-sensitive systems such as authorization, authentication, token management, credential storage, or related platforms. You bring a systems-thinking mindset and enjoy solving complex engineering challenges that span client and backend technologies. You have a solid understanding of software architecture, secure system design, and modern authorization protocols such as OAuth 2.0. You approach problems thoughtfully, with strong attention to detail and a focus on building secure, reliable, and maintainable solutions. You communicate clearly and enjoy collaborating with engineers across multiple teams and technical disciplines. You have experience working with shared cross-platform codebases and understand how native platform layers interact with common C++ libraries. You enjoy working on large-scale distributed systems where your contributions improve experiences for hundreds of millions of Spotify users.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in London or Stockholm. We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.
 
At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

rows.description:
We design Spotify’s consumer experience—end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints—from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify. We own music content ingestion at Spotify, which is how music from labels, distributors and other partners gets onto the platform. We receive industry-standard deliveries, validate them, and turn them into the catalog data that teams across Spotify build on, including lyrics, rights and supply data. As we add new content types and partners, we’re building an ingestion platform that scales without a custom build every time.

What You'll Do:
Build and run the backend services and data pipelines that ingest, validate and process music deliveries from partners, covering audio, metadata, lyrics and new content types Own large parts of the ingestion pipeline and lead technical work as we add video, richer partner data and other new content Make ingestion more reliable, catch data quality problems at the point of entry, and improve the operational tooling around the pipeline Design and evolve APIs and schemas that other teams depend on, keeping contracts stable and backward compatible Help move validation towards real time and make Silk Road a well-documented, self-serve platform Deliver roadmap work, take part in planning, review code, and share on-call Work with Content Ops, operations tooling teams, partner teams and the product teams that build on our content

Who You Are:
You have strong experience building and operating backend services and data pipelines in production at scale, ideally in Java, Scala or Go You have designed APIs and handled schema evolution and backward compatibility in systems where other teams rely on stable contracts You’re comfortable modelling data for auditability, versioning and efficient querying and  understand the tradeoffs between real-time and batch processing You lead projects from discovery to handover, make sound technical decisions, and mentor others You may have worked with content ingestion, metadata standards such as DDEX, B2B partner integrations, rights or compliance-sensitive data, lyrics or time-synced data, or GCP.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in London or Stockholm. We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Our team pioneers and advances state-of-the-art generative technologies for music that create breakthrough experiences for fans and artists. We invent entirely new listening experiences that center and celebrate artists and creatives. All of our products will put artists and songwriters first, through these four principles:
Partnerships with record labels, distributors, and music publishers: We’ll develop new products for artists and fans through upfront agreements, not by asking for forgiveness later.
Choice in participation: We recognize there’s a wide range of views on the use of generative music tools within the artistic community. Therefore, artists and rightsholders will choose if and how to participate to ensure the use of AI tools aligns with the values of the people behind the music.
Fair compensation and new revenue: We will build products that create wholly new revenue streams for rightsholders, artists, and songwriters, ensuring they are properly compensated for the use of their work and transparently credited for their contributions.
Artist-fan connection: AI tools we develop will not replace human artistry. They will give artists new ways to be creative and connect with fans. We will leverage our role as the place where more than 700 million people already come to listen to music every month to ensure that generative AI deepens artist-fan connections.
Learn more in our press release: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-10-16/artist-first-ai-music-spotify-collaboration/

What You'll Do:
Conduct groundbreaking research in generative audio using diffusion or flow matching models, with a focus on one or more of the following areas:   Vocal Synthesis — Research in vocal and speech synthesis, along with related areas such as ML-based audio processing and signal processing.   Post-Training — Research in post-training techniques for music generation, including preference alignment methods (such as DPO, RLHF, or KTO), reward model design and training, and reinforcement learning to improve output quality, controllability, and human preference adherence.   Editing — Research in iterative music generation and audio editing, including capabilities such as stem replacement, instrumentation change, mood changes (while preserving content), tempo changes, and structure changes.   You will also: Run large-scale experiments with access to Spotify's extensive infrastructure and an audience of more than 700 million monthly active users. Create practical applications that harness generative technologies and push the boundaries of what's possible in listening experiences. Collaborate as part of a cross-functional team—working closely with scientists, engineers, product managers, designers, user researchers, and analysts—to craft innovative solutions to complex challenges. Have a direct impact on Spotify's products, tools, and services, working on projects that influence the entire organization. Engage with the broader research community by publishing your findings, delivering talks, and attending top conferences.

You have a Ph.D. in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field. Previous industry experience is helpful. Every dataset at Spotify, from the data behind creator royalties to the signals powering recommendations, is registered, published and traced through systems our team builds. We're the source of truth for what data exists at Spotify, where it lives, who owns it, and how it flows from one pipeline to the next.
These systems sit on the critical path of the platform. Data teams use them every day to publish and find data, and other platform teams build on them for access, retention, governance and incident response. That means our work is judged on correctness and reliability, because every system built on top of ours is only as good as the metadata we provide.
This is a backend role focused on data management, working on the problems at the core of any large data platform: running a data catalog that stays accurate at scale, capturing lineage across batch and streaming workloads, managing schemas as they evolve, and guaranteeing that consumers only read complete data. We build on open standards like OpenLineage and Apache Iceberg, and define the internal standards for naming, storage and metadata that the rest of Spotify builds against. As the platform takes on new storage technologies and new kinds of data assets, those standards and the systems behind them have to evolve with it, and you'll help decide how.

What You'll Do:
Build and Evolve Core Services: Design, build and operate the backend services and APIs behind our data catalog, lineage and publishing systems, and evolve them as the platform adopts new storage technologies and new kinds of data. Hold them to a high bar for correctness, performance and reliability. Build Data Pipelines: Develop and run the batch and streaming pipelines that keep our metadata current, processing platform events and audit logs to capture how data is created and changed, and turning lineage and metadata into data products other teams build on. Own Projects End to End: Turn what the teams using our platform need into technical designs, drive them through delivery and rollout, and own the results once they're in production. Keep the Platform Healthy: Take part in on-call for critical services, build in observability and quality checks by default, and use automation, including AI tooling, to reduce toil for the team and our users.

Who You Are:
You have solid experience building and running backend services and APIs in production with Java, and you care about API design, versioning and backward compatibility. You're comfortable with SQL and have worked with data pipelines or a cloud data warehouse such as BigQuery, Snowflake or Databricks. Hands-on experience with batch or streaming frameworks like Beam, Flink or Spark is a plus. You have a working understanding of data engineering concepts such as orchestration, metadata management, data quality, governance and lineage. You break problems down into clear, shippable steps, reasoning through tradeoffs and risks and converging on clear recommendations. You own the quality of what you ship, including code written with AI assistance, and you care about operating it well after launch. You are a strong communicator and collaborator who enjoys working across teams, and you're comfortable in a dynamic platform environment where many engineers depend on what you build and priorities evolve with the business.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in Stockholm or London. We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Spotify Technology is our business-to-business software team, helping organizations improve how they build and deliver software. Our products, including Backstage Portal, Confidence, and Xirp, support developers and AI-powered systems as they navigate increasingly complex engineering environments.
As Revenue Operations Manager, you'll own revenue operations for Spotify Technology, helping our sales organization scale from early growth to a mature, segmented go-to-market model. This is a hands-on role where you'll work closely with the business day to day, identify challenges early, and build the systems, processes, and insights that enable sustainable growth.
You'll partner with Sales leadership, Marketing, Sales Engineering, and Customer Success to improve how we operate across the customer lifecycle. You'll balance strategic planning with practical execution, creating structure that helps our teams work efficiently as the business evolves.

What You'll Do:
• Own sales operations for Spotify Technology, including CRM, pipeline management, forecasting, territory and account assignment, and deal desk processes. • Design and roll out a segmented sales model that evolves our go-to-market approach as the business matures. • Build infrastructure and systems to support a scalable Commercial sales motion (companies with fewer than 1,000 employees), focused on faster deal cycles, efficient lead routing, and repeatable processes. • Build infrastructure and systems to support a strategic Enterprise sales motion (companies with 1,000+ employees), enabling prospecting, account planning, and multi-product engagements. • Partner with the Director of Sales as a strategic advisor on quota setting, capacity planning, compensation, territory design, and headcount modeling. • Support revenue across the full customer lifecycle, including new business, expansion, and retention. • Build reporting and dashboards to track pipeline coverage, conversion rates, time to close, forecast accuracy, and net revenue retention by segment. • Strengthen forecasting discipline and maintain a healthy, predictable pipeline through effective reporting and sales processes. • Identify friction across the sales process, including handoffs between Account Executives, Sales Engineering, and Customer Success, and drive improvements with cross-functional partners. • Partner with Marketing on pipeline generation reporting, lead management, and process improvements. • Establish and continuously improve operating rhythms, including forecast calls, pipeline reviews, and quarterly business reviews (QBRs), as the business scales. • Evaluate and manage the go-to-market (GTM) technology stack to support efficient and scalable sales operations.

Who You Are:
• You have 6+ years of experience in revenue operations, sales operations, or go-to-market strategy, with a track record of meaningful impact at a senior level. • You have experience scaling sales operations through a startup or high-growth phase and understand when to introduce new processes and structure. • You can build systems and processes from the ground up without adding unnecessary complexity. • You are proficient in using AI and can lead initiatives that improve sales effectiveness through AI-enabled tools and processes. • You have experience in B2B SaaS, ideally within developer platforms, DevOps tools, or cloud services. • You understand the differences between product-led growth (PLG), Commercial, and Enterprise sales motions and have experience designing segmented sales models. • You understand complex technical sales involving Sales Engineering and recognize the importance of customer retention and post-sale success in revenue strategy. • You have hands-on experience with Salesforce or a similar CRM, including building reports, workflows, and resolving data issues. • You use data to guide forecasting, capacity modeling, and funnel analysis, combining analytical skills with sound business judgment. • You can influence senior sales leaders, build alignment across teams, and drive decisions without formal authority. • You are comfortable working in evolving environments, adapting as priorities change, and helping shape how an innovative business grows.

Where You'll Be:
• This role is based in London • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.
At Spotify, security helps make innovation possible. Our Enterprise Security team protects the systems and technology that support our employees and the more than 700 million people who use Spotify. We're looking for a Security Engineer to help strengthen our enterprise security across identity, devices, networks, and AI-powered tools. You'll build practical solutions, work with teams across the business, and help us create a secure environment where people can do their best work.

What You'll Do:
Improve enterprise security by identifying risks and implementing solutions that protect Spotify while supporting a great employee experience. Design and build security tools, integrations, and automation to make security processes more effective and scalable. Analyze security data to identify gaps, understand emerging risks, and guide improvements. Implement security controls across identity and access management, enterprise applications, endpoints, and cloud-based services. Assess security risks associated with AI tools and agents, and help develop safeguards that support responsible adoption. Collaborate with IT, infrastructure, and security teams to strengthen security across devices, networks, and enterprise systems. Evaluate and improve enterprise security technologies, including managed browsers and device security tools. Share your expertise and work with colleagues across technical and non-technical teams to make security practices clear, practical, and effective.

Who You Are:
You are a security engineer with experience in securing a fast moving technology company. Alternatively, you have expertise in enterprise systems engineering and are ready to transition into a security-focused career. You have demonstrated experience applying enterprise security principles across IAM, SSO, networking, and device management, and you understand how these domains interrelate to form a cohesive security foundation. You can think like an attacker and understand how to identify risks and implement countermeasures against threats that span identity, endpoint, network, and cloud boundaries. You have a solid understanding of the risks introduced by agentic AI in an enterprise context and you are keen to get hands-on identifying and mitigating these risks in our environment. You actively leverage AI tooling to augment your own work and are eager to explore how emerging AI capabilities can be applied to enterprise security challenges. You can critically evaluate tools, practices and procedures, and you're willing to advocate for improvements and change when you see opportunities or risk.    You have an understanding of the current threat landscape, and want to be part of a team creating and implementing state of the art security solutions in an AI-enabled enterprise environment. You communicate complex security topics clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences, and you're comfortable working across a global, cross-functional organization. You thrive in a flexible environment with broad scope and you're energized by the freedom to innovate and challenge conventional security thinking.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in Stockholm or London We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.
 
At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

Join Spotify's Japan Growth team and help more listeners discover the value of Spotify Premium. As part of our Markets & Subscriptions organisation, you'll play a key role in growing our subscriber base in one of Spotify's most important markets. Japan is Spotify's only single-country region, and we're entering an exciting new chapter focused on partnerships and sustainable growth. Working across marketing, product, data and commercial teams, you'll shape our growth strategy, turn customer insights into action and find new ways to connect Japanese listeners with Spotify Premium. You'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while developing your leadership responsibilities over time.

What You'll Do:
Lead Spotify's growth strategy in Japan, driving Premium subscriber acquisition, conversion, retention and revenue performance. Own and deliver the Premium growth plan, identifying opportunities across the customer journey and translating them into measurable business outcomes. Work closely with Marketing, Music and Partnerships leadership to shape growth priorities based on consumer insights, market trends and competitive dynamics. Partner with our Partnerships team to unlock subscriber growth through telecommunications, device, payment and content partners. Design and run experiments across paid, owned and in-app channels, using data and clear success metrics to improve conversion and retention. Develop CRM and lifecycle marketing strategies across email, push notifications and in-app messaging, creating relevant experiences that engage and retain listeners. Collaborate with Product, Data Science, Payments and Finance teams to build business cases, evaluate performance and identify scalable growth opportunities. Lead and develop a team member, share learnings with regional Growth teams and explore how AI-powered tools can improve decision-making and execution.

Who You Are:
You have experience driving growth in a digital consumer business, such as streaming, entertainment, e-commerce or consumer technology. You have a track record of owning subscriber or commercial growth targets and understand how acquisition, conversion and retention contribute to sustainable growth. You're experienced in digital marketing, CRM and lifecycle campaigns, with the ability to turn customer insights into meaningful action. You're confident using data, analytics tools and experimentation to make decisions, evaluate performance and identify opportunities. Familiarity with SQL can help you go further. You understand subscription business economics, including customer lifetime value, subscriber acquisition cost and gross margin. You combine analytical thinking with creative marketing instincts and a strong understanding of Japanese consumer behaviour and culture. You're comfortable collaborating across functions, influencing stakeholders and taking ownership of initiatives in a fast-moving environment. You enjoy developing others, are curious about using AI to improve how you work, and communicate fluently in Japanese and confidently in business English. rows.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.About the role As an AV Engineer focused on builds and design, you'll design and implement the systems that enable world-class collaboration and communication across offices. This role is critical as we rapidly expand our physical footprint, with plans for multiple new offices and expansions over the coming years. You'll be responsible for architecting AV solutions from concept through commissioning, ensuring our conference rooms, event spaces, and collaboration areas provide frictionless experiences that enable our teams to advance AI safety research. You'll help establish standards and systems that scale efficiently while pushing the boundaries of what's possible in workplace collaboration technology. This is an opportunity to shape how a cutting-edge AI research organization communicates and collaborates, building infrastructure that supports everything from small team meetings to company-wide all-hands broadcasts reaching thousands of remote participants. Responsibilities Lead AV design, procurement, and programming for new office builds, expansions, and retrofits across our global portfolio Create and maintain AV system designs including schematic drawings, line diagrams, and elevation plans Program and commission AV systems to meet specific use cases and user requirements Execute successful "first day of business" deployments for new offices, ensuring all systems are operational for day-one occupancy Attend build coordination meetings with architects, contractors, and workplace teams to drive AV requirements and integration Innovate and test emerging AV technologies to optimize productivity and enable premium experiences for existing and upcoming spaces Develop automated solutions to improve system reliability and reduce operational overhead Partner with Security and IT teams to ensure AV systems meet enterprise security requirements Create comprehensive documentation for all systems including programming logic, troubleshooting guides, and operational procedures Oversee operations globally to ensure seamless AV operations and service delivery standards are consistently met Manage relationships with AV integrators and vendors to ensure project success Assist with AV operations support including event production and system maintenance as needed You may be a good fit if you Have 8+ years of experience designing and implementing AV systems in an enterprise environment Are proficient in control system programming utilizing the Q-Sys ecosystem or similar Have hands-on experience with video conferencing platforms, particularly Google Meet Can read and create AV technical drawings including schematics, line diagrams, and rack elevations Understand digital signal processing (DSP) concepts for audio, including acoustic echo cancellation, noise reduction, EQ/dynamics, and automixing Are familiar with enterprise video distribution, streaming technologies, and broadcast standards Can manage multiple projects simultaneously while meeting aggressive timelines Collaborate effectively with non-technical stakeholders to translate requirements into technical solutions Have excellent troubleshooting skills and are comfortable diving into complex integrated systems Care about creating exceptional user experiences through technology Are excited about the opportunity to build scalable AV infrastructure from the ground up Strong candidates may also have Experience with Logitech video conferencing ecosystem and management platforms Certifications such as Q-Sys Level 2, CTS, or CTS-D Familiarity with control scripts using Lua within Q-Sys Background in broadcast production or live event engineering Experience with Netgear network switches running AV over IP systems (QLAN, Dante, SMPTE 2110) Familiarity with digital signage platforms (Appspace or similar) Understanding of acoustical design principles for conference spaces Track record of successful large-scale office technology deployments Previous experience performing AV installations Background working in high-growth technology companies Experience with Google Workspace administration Role Specific Location Policy: This role will be based in our London office This role is expected to be in office 75% of the time This position will require up to 8 weeks of domestic and international travel to help with new office build outs Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be received on a rolling basis.The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.Annual Salary:£210,000—£250,000 GBPLogistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

rows.description:
We are seeking Research Scientists (across all levels of seniority) to join our Artist-First AI Music Lab. Our team pioneers and advances state-of-the-art generative technologies for music that create breakthrough experiences for fans and artists. We invent entirely new listening experiences that center and celebrate artists and creatives. All of our products will put artists and songwriters first, through these four principles:
Partnerships with record labels, distributors, and music publishers: We’ll develop new products for artists and fans through upfront agreements, not by asking for forgiveness later.
Choice in participation: We recognize there’s a wide range of views on the use of generative music tools within the artistic community. Therefore, artists and rightsholders will choose if and how to participate to ensure the use of AI tools aligns with the values of the people behind the music.
Fair compensation and new revenue: We will build products that create wholly new revenue streams for rightsholders, artists, and songwriters, ensuring they are properly compensated for the use of their work and transparently credited for their contributions.
Artist-fan connection: AI tools we develop will not replace human artistry. They will give artists new ways to be creative and connect with fans. We will leverage our role as the place where more than 700 million people already come to listen to music every month to ensure that generative AI deepens artist-fan connections.
Learn more in our press release: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-10-16/artist-first-ai-music-spotify-collaboration/

What You'll Do:
Conduct groundbreaking research in generative audio using diffusion or flow matching models, with a focus on one or more of the following areas:   Vocal Synthesis — Research in vocal and speech synthesis, along with related areas such as ML-based audio processing and signal processing.   Post-Training — Research in post-training techniques for music generation, including preference alignment methods (such as DPO, RLHF, or KTO), reward model design and training, and reinforcement learning to improve output quality, controllability, and human preference adherence.   Editing — Research in iterative music generation and audio editing, including capabilities such as stem replacement, instrumentation change, mood changes (while preserving content), tempo changes, and structure changes.   You will also: Run large-scale experiments with access to Spotify's extensive infrastructure and an audience of more than 700 million monthly active users. Create practical applications that harness generative technologies and push the boundaries of what's possible in listening experiences. Collaborate as part of a cross-functional team—working closely with scientists, engineers, product managers, designers, user researchers, and analysts—to craft innovative solutions to complex challenges. Have a direct impact on Spotify's products, tools, and services, working on projects that influence the entire organization. Engage with the broader research community by publishing your findings, delivering talks, and attending top conferences.

Who You Are:
You have a Ph.D. in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field. Previous industry experience is helpful. You have experience in one or more of the following fields: generative modeling, machine learning, music information retrieval, speech processing, audio processing, signal processing, probabilistic modeling, computer vision, or related areas. You have deep expertise in at least one of the focus areas above—whether that's vocal/speech synthesis, post-training alignment techniques (e.g., PPO, GRPO, DPO), or audio-to-audio generation and text-guided music editing. rows.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.About the role As a Deployment Manager on the Beneficial Deployments team, you will guide customers from a signed contract into a live, governed, and adopted deployment so that customers achieve tangible impact rather than simply incremental improvement with Claude. You'll guide organizations from contract signature to production deployment across Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, and our API products, fundamentally changing how they work and deliver on their missions. You'll be the technical hands that switch Claude on. Before any organization can drive adoption, before any champion can ship their first workflow, someone has to connect Claude to the customer's identity provider, get the right people provisioned into the right workspaces, and walk their CISO through how it all comes together. That's your work. You turn "we've signed the contract" into "our employees can log in, with the right access, under the right policies, the way our security team expects." This is a high-leverage role where you'll pioneer scalable activation methodologies that enable hundreds of nonprofit customers to unlock transformative use cases and realize measurable outcomes at unprecedented speed. You won't just follow playbooks. You'll design the frameworks and repeatable processes that can be deployed consistently across diverse customer environments, and you'll shape them into programs that reach customers we could never serve one at a time. You'll operate at the intersection of technical deployment, enablement, and program design. Some days you'll be in the weeds with a customer's IT team debugging a SAML assertion; other days you'll be stepping back to ask how the last ten deployments should change the next hundred. Your systems-thinking approach will directly shape how we activate customers, and your strategic management will ensure every customer achieves meaningful outcomes within their first 90 days. By identifying patterns across activations, you'll build replicable approaches to organizational change while maintaining the agility to customize solutions for each customer's unique transformation journey. Responsibilities: Own the complete activation journey from contract signature to production deployment, orchestrating cross-functional resources and customer teams to ensure rapid time-to-value across Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, and API products. Deploy Claude inside customer environments. Configure and troubleshoot SSO (SAML), SCIM and JIT provisioning, MCP connectors, admin policy templates, and seat-assignment logic across Okta, Entra ID, Ping, and Google Workspace. Deliver informative transitions to Support for deeper issues that require investigation or engineering support. Act as a trusted advisor to customer CISOs and CTOs on governance and enterprise setup. Bring a clear point of view on best practices, help security and IT leadership make the design decisions that determine whether a deployment holds up over time Light up the capabilities that make Claude valuable. Enable and govern MCP connectors to the customer's systems, ensure Skills, Projects, and other capabilities are turned on and configured for their use cases, and work with their IT team on the approvals and OAuth consent this requires, so that day one feels ready Design and scale activation frameworks by identifying patterns across deployments and building templated playbooks that balance standardization with customization for breakthrough outcomes. Turn playbooks into programs. Package what works into repeatable, increasingly self-serve motions (deployment checklists, admin enablement sessions, onboarding cohorts, Claude-powered guidance) so that activation quality no longer depends on you being in the room. Drive organizational transformation by developing change management strategies, rollout plans, and Train-the-Trainer programs that build internal AI champions and catalyze adoption across customer organizations. Define and track success metrics across activation rate, time-to-value, customer satisfaction, and operational efficiency, using data to continuously optimize the motion. Channel customer insights back to Product, Support, and Security teams, serving as voice of the customer so that repeat deployment blockers get solved once. You may be a good fit if you have: 5+ years in customer-facing technical roles such as implementation management, technical account management, technical onboarding, solutions consulting, or customer success, with a track record of running multiple concurrent enterprise deployments with documented handoffs. Experience serving nonprofits or mission-driven organizations. You've worked with (or inside) them and you understand how they differ from commercial enterprises. Hands-on, sustained ownership of enterprise identity integration work. SAML, OIDC, SCIM v2, and JIT provisioning across at least two major identity providers (Okta, Entra ID, Ping, Google Workspace). You can debug a broken SAML assertion or a misconfigured SCIM attribute map without escalating, and you know when a Support handoff is the right call. Experience advising CISOs, CTOs, or IT leadership on enterprise governance and setup for a SaaS or AI platform, with an informed point of view on org topology, access models, RBAC, and OAuth. Working knowledge of security and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR) sufficient to anticipate what a customer's security review will ask, and to know when to bring in our AI Security Specialist. You've designed, shipped, and measured programs that serve many customers at once: onboarding cohorts, enablement series, admin academies, lifecycle or engagement motions. You naturally ask "how might we scale this?", turn 1:1 moments into 1:many programs, and instrument what you build so you know what's working. Hands-on fluency with AI in your own workflow. You've prototyped, generated content, analyzed accounts, or replaced internal processes with LLMs, and you can talk concretely about what worked, what didn't, and what's next. You don't wait for AI tooling to arrive; you build it. Organizational change and enablement experience including developing rollout strategies, navigating stakeholder resistance, building internal champions, and designing programs that drive adoption at scale. Comfort building in ambiguity. This is a new role on the team, and what you build becomes the template. You'll thrive creating structure where none exists, adapting quickly as the business evolves, and learning continuously. Data-driven and metrics-oriented. Experience setting and tracking success metrics from day one, using data to optimize approaches, and demonstrating impact to diverse stakeholders. raw_data.position: Member of Technical Staff Applied ML RecSys
raw_data.description:
About Liquid AI

Spun out of MIT CSAIL, we build general-purpose AI systems that run efficiently across deployment targets, from data center accelerators to on-device hardware, ensuring low latency, minimal memory usage, privacy, and reliability. We partner with enterprises across consumer electronics, automotive, life sciences, and financial services. We are scaling rapidly and need exceptional people to help us get there.

The Opportunity

This is a rare chance to apply frontier sequential recommendation architectures to real enterprise problems at scale. You will own applied ML work end-to-end for recommendation system workloads, adapting Liquid Foundation Models for customers who need personalization and ranking capabilities that run efficiently under production constraints.

Unlike most recommendation roles that are siloed into a single product surface, this role gives you full ownership over how large-scale recommendation models are adapted, evaluated, and deployed for enterprise customers. Between engagements, you will build reusable applied tooling and workflows that accelerate future delivery.

If you care about data quality at scale, user behavior modeling, and making recommendation systems actually work in enterprise production environments, this is the role.

What Weâre Looking For

We need someone who:

  • Takes ownership: Owns customer recommendation system engagements end-to-end, from requirements through delivery and evaluation.

  • Thinks at scale: Can reason about user interaction data, sequential modeling, feature engineering, and evaluation across large-scale production systems.

  • Is pragmatic: Optimizes for measurable customer outcomes (engagement, conversion, revenue lift) over theoretical novelty.

  • Communicates clearly: Can translate between customer business metrics and internal technical decisions, and push back when needed.

The Work

  • Act as the technical owner for enterprise customer engagements involving recommendation and ranking workloads

  • Translate customer requirements into concrete specifications for recommendation models

  • Design and execute data pipelines for user interaction data, feature engineering, and training data curation at scale

  • Fine-tune and adapt large-scale sequential recommendation models (e.g., HSTU-style architectures) for customer-specific use cases

  • Design task-specific evaluations for recommendation model performance (ranking quality, latency, throughput) and interpret results

  • Build reusable applied tooling and workflows that accelerate future customer engagements

Desired Experience

Must-have:

  • Hands-on experience building or fine-tuning recommendation models at scale (not just off-the-shelf collaborative filtering)

  • Experience with sequential recommendation architectures, user behavior modeling, or large-scale ranking systems

  • Strong intuition for data quality and evaluation design in recommendation contexts (offline metrics, A/B testing, business metric alignment)

  • Experience with large-scale data pipelines for user interaction data and feature engineering

  • Proficiency in Python and PyTorch with autonomous coding and debugging ability

Nice-to-have:

  • Experience with transformer-based recommendation architectures (HSTU, SASRec, BERT4Rec, or similar)

  • Experience delivering recommendation systems to external customers with measurable business outcomes

  • Familiarity with serving recommendation models under latency and throughput constraints

What Success Looks Like (Year One)

  • Independently owns and delivers enterprise recommendation system engagements with minimal oversight

  • Is trusted by customers as the technical owner, demonstrating strong judgment on the tradeoffs between model quality, latency, and business impact

  • Has built reusable applied workflows or tooling that accelerate future customer engagements

What We Offer

  • Real ML work: You will build and adapt large-scale recommendation models for enterprise customers, working with frontier architectures like HSTU under real production constraints.

  • Compensation: Competitive base salary with equity in a unicorn-stage company

  • Health: We pay 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for employees and dependents

  • Financial: 401(k) matching up to 4% of base pay

  • Time Off: Unlimited PTO plus company-wide Refill Days throughout the year

rows.description:
Sell what you love. For us and millions of users across the globe, that’s Spotify. Join the Sales team and you’ll build the relationships that help grow our business in existing markets and beyond. We don’t just sell creative solutions to our clients and partners, we help to shape them; using our expert knowledge of ad products, sales channels and the industry to impact the way the world experiences music and podcasts. 


Our Revenue Growth team drives advertiser acquisition and retention at scale by turning data into action. We build and run scalable go-to-market programs that help advertisers succeed, through lifecycle communications and seller-facing actions. 
As a Senior Program Analyst - GTM Ops, you'll own the technical layer that makes Revenue Growth actually run. Working within Spotify's broader data infrastructure, you'll build the team-specific tools, endpoints, and pipelines our programs depend on — the reporting that helps sellers act, the data feeds that power our advertiser tools, the pipelines that keep everything moving. Your work won't be abstract; it shows up directly in what the team ships and what sellers experience.

What You’ll Do:
Work on high-impact data problems that support revenue growth and help our advertising business scale Build and maintain dbt models and BigQuery pipelines that power team tools and seller-facing reporting Monitor pipeline health, identify issues early, and partner with data engineering and Insights teams to resolve upstream challenges Create dashboards and reports that sales teams rely on, translating business needs into clear, actionable views Partner closely with sales teams and leadership to understand needs, scope solutions, and deliver data that supports prioritization and decision-making Improve how data is used in the sales process by surfacing signals that help teams focus, personalize outreach, and close opportunities Support and extend pipelines that process unstructured data using LLMs, ensuring outputs are reliable, validated, and usable within BigQuery

Who You Are:
You have 4+ years of experience in analytics engineering, BI engineering, or data/reporting roles, ideally supporting go-to-market, growth, or sales teams You are experienced with SQL and BigQuery, and build with reliability and maintainability in mind You have worked with dbt and understand how to extend and maintain models within an existing DAG You enjoy building systems that work consistently for a team and take pride in operational reliability You communicate clearly and can partner directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand needs and deliver solutions You are comfortable translating business questions into structured data outputs and reporting You are curious about applying AI in data workflows, including working with or learning about LLM-driven pipelines

Where You’ll Be:
This role is based in New York City. We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

The United States base range for this position is $92,293 - 131,847, plus equity. The benefits available for this position include health insurance, six-month paid parental leave, 401(k) retirement plan, monthly meal allowance, 23 paid days off, 13 paid flexible holidays, paid sick leave. These ranges may be modified in the future.


Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.
 
At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.
