GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. *Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.An overview of this role As an Strategic Account Executive, you’ll help expand GitLab’s presence across the Public Sector in Brazil by building trusted relationships with senior leaders at large organizations and guiding them through complex platform decisions. You’ll use a consultative sales approach to connect customer business needs with our AI-powered DevSecOps platform, helping teams improve developer productivity, reduce security and compliance risk, and move software delivery forward with more confidence. In this role, you’ll support strategic accounts across the full customer journey, from early conversations through adoption, while helping us position GitLab as a leading DevSecOps partner in the Brazilian market. You’ll work across pre-sales, post-sales, partner, marketing, and support teams, and we’ll rely on you to bring strong account leadership, customer outcomes, and clear communication in English and Portuguese. Over your first year, your impact will come from building account plans for large organizations, developing new opportunities, and helping customers successfully adopt GitLab in ways that align to their business goals. What you’ll do Lead strategic account activity for prospects and customers across the Public Sector in Brazil, providing direction throughout pre-sales and post-sales engagements. Develop opportunities within Public Sector accounts through prospecting, relationship building, and a consultative understanding of customer business needs. Create account plans and customer proposals that clearly connect GitLab capabilities to organizational priorities and transformation goals. Coordinate with pre-sales, post-sales, and support teams to support successful product rollout and customer adoption. Generate qualified pipeline in partnership with strategic channel partners and support new customer development efforts. Contribute customer feedback and product ideas to GitLab’s public issue tracker to represent the voice of the customer. Prepare activity and forecast reports, and help analyze wins and losses to improve future sales execution. Collaborate with marketing, account teams, product managers, and technical teams to share lessons learned and communicate customer needs clearly. Strength in negotiation, presentation, and closing conversations in a clear and effective way. Comfort working independently on complex projects while coordinating with cross-functional teams. Fluency in English and Portuguese for customer-facing and internal communication. Familiarity with GitLab or related tools, including Git, software development tools, application lifecycle management, or security and application security tools. Alignment with GitLab’s values, with openness to transferable experience from adjacent technical or software environments. About the team The team focuses on growing GitLab’s Public Sector business in Brazil by helping organizations adopt a single platform for software delivery, security, and collaboration. This role works closely with cross-functional partners across sales, solutions, support, marketing, and product, and contributes to an asynchronous, distributed way of working that values transparency, accountability, and shared customer insight. raw_data.title: People Technology Analyst - Workday

rows.description:
Spotify’s mission is to unlock the potential of human creativity by giving a million creative artists the opportunity to live off their art and billions of fans the chance to enjoy and be passionate about these creators.
Data is a means to an end, and Spotify extracts value from data through application. The Data Platform Studio helps Spotify win by enabling the application of data in an intuitive and efficient way.
Data Platform is responsible for how data is collected, processed, stored, governed, and made available to the thousands of engineers, data scientists, analysts, and machine learning practitioners who build Spotify’s products. As AI agents increasingly generate code, write data pipelines, and power personalized user experiences, Data Platform sits at the center of one of the most important infrastructure domains at Spotify.
We're looking for a passionate Product Manager to join the team responsible for Spotify’s data catalogue, metadata, and data lineage capabilities. In this role, you'll own the strategy and roadmap for a critical part of Spotify's data ecosystem, helping users discover, understand, trust, and safely use data at scale. You'll work closely with engineers, designers, data scientists, and product teams across Spotify to make working with data faster, safer, and more intuitive.

What You'll Do:
Develop and own the product strategy and roadmap for Spotify's data catalogue, metadata, and data lineage domain. Diagnose and deeply understand the needs of Spotify's data community, including data engineers, data scientists, analysts, ML engineers, and increasingly AI agents. Identify and prioritize the highest-impact problems to solve, balancing user needs, business priorities, platform requirements, and regulatory considerations. Evaluate and deliver solutions through building, buying, or integrating third-party products and capabilities. Define success metrics and KPIs that measure adoption, value creation, and business impact. Build strong relationships with internal product, engineering, analytics, and data teams to understand workflows, gather feedback, and shape future platform investments. Collaborate closely with engineering, design, and data science partners to deliver high-quality platform experiences. Influence stakeholders across the Data Platform Studio and broader Spotify organization to align around product direction and priorities. Help shape how Spotify approaches metadata, governance, discoverability, lineage, and trust in an increasingly AI-driven world. Stay informed on industry trends across data platforms, developer tools, AI/ML infrastructure, analytics, and data governance.

Who You Are:
You have 2+ years of Product Management experience, ideally working on platform products, developer tools, data infrastructure, analytics platforms, or data governance systems. You have a technical foundation through a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, and/or prior experience in engineering or technical roles. You are comfortable working with engineers and can engage in technical discussions while representing customer and business needs. You are an excellent communicator and collaborator who can build alignment across teams with different priorities and levels of technical expertise. You have strong systems-thinking skills and can connect workflows, platforms, users, and business outcomes. You have empathy for people who work with data and understand the challenges they face every day. You enjoy working through ambiguity, breaking down complex problems, and creating clarity for teams. You are curious about how AI is transforming the data landscape and are excited to help shape that future. You lead with humility, build trust through collaboration, and help teams move forward with focus and momentum.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in London or Stockholm We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

rows.description:
Sell what you love. For us and millions of users across the globe, that’s Spotify. Join the Sales team and you’ll build the relationships that help grow our business in existing markets and beyond. We don’t just sell creative solutions to our clients and partners, we help to shape them; using our expert knowledge of ad products, sales channels and the industry to impact the way the world experiences music and podcasts. 


Spotify is expanding our Agency development team dedicated to driving new and innovative strategic partnerships with our largest agency partners in France. You will showcase all the technological and data assets available to drive business goals.
The Agency Development Lead will own strategic agency partnerships across the French market. This is not an account management role — you'll architect the agency relationships and commercial frameworks which create opportunities for the FR sales team to activate. You bring deep experience in partnership development and senior agency relationships at the holding company level, with an established track record of building long-term consultative solutions and innovative ways of working with agencies which create value for advertisers.  You have a passion for digital media, music, podcasts and innovation, and you know how to translate that into commercial strategy.

What You'll Do:
Be the primary liaison, internal advocate and thought leader representing Spotify with a specific focus on key C-Level relationships, in partnership with the Sales leadership team in France. Design and negotiate commercial frameworks (incentive structures, commitments, preferred partner terms), key initiatives and areas of focus that align with Spotify solutions to drive innovation, data activation, insights, research and audio engagement Own agency contact mapping, business reviews, education plans, and communication across assigned agencies  Partner with Agency Commercial, Activation, and Product teams to accelerate adoption of Spotify's automation, self-service, and programmatic buying solutions — ensuring commercial strategy and execution are aligned to prioritized business goals. Ensure strategic alignment across the FR sales org on agency priorities, partnership terms, and key commercial developments — acting as the connective tissue between agency partners and internal teams. Own the commercial narrative across the agency portfolio — tracking revenue trends, spending patterns, and emerging client opportunities to inform partnership strategy and proactively recommend corrective measures to global, regional, and local sales leadership. Structure and develop a strategic agency narrative — grounded in emerging areas like Ads Manager, programmatic, measurement, data collaboration, AI-enabled workflows, and evolving agency operating models — to drive growth and adoption of Spotify's portfolio of solutions across our holding company partnerships. rows.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.About the Role Anthropic runs one of the largest and fastest-growing infrastructure fleets in the industry, across multiple accelerator families, CPU families, clouds, neoclouds, and on-prem sites. Capacity Engineering owns the data, tooling, and systems that let Anthropic plan, measure, and maximize utilization of that fleet: we partner on supply deals, wire telemetry from day zero, own the canonical capacity data layer, and build the planning and enforcement tools every research and product team relies on. This role sits in the Planning pillar, on the Demand Planning team, and works daily with research engineering, pretraining, inference, compute supply, finance, and external vendors. You own the tranches. The job has two halves that feed each other. Upstream, you take the Demand Planning forecast and turn it into per-tranche requirements — shape, interconnect, region, supporting resources, date — and carry those into sourcing negotiations and data center build reviews so we contract for capacity we can actually use when we need it. Downstream, you own the integrated schedule and system of record for every tranche in flight — from contracted through reserved, ingested, in-cluster, healthy, and occupied — and you drive the owners of each hop to their dates. Every slip you see downstream becomes a contract-language fix, an automation, or a correction fed back to the forecast. What you'll do Turn the forecast into per-tranche requirements. Take the Demand Planning forecast plus direct input from research, pretraining, and inference planners, and convert it into concrete accelerator, interconnect, region, supporting-resource, and date requirements for each tranche. Represent those in sourcing negotiations and data center build reviews, including which contractual terms actually move delivery dates. Qualify tranches for deliverability before signature. The Capacity Planner signs fit-to-forecast; you sign whether the shape can land schedulable, healthy, and instrumented in that region on that date, with storage, egress, identity in place. Close the delivery loop. Track forecast-versus-delivered on shape, region, and timing for every tranche; publish the variance; and feed it back to Demand Planning and into the next contract. Own the bring-up system of record. Define the canonical contract-to-occupied state machine with explicit entry and exit criteria per stage, and make it a first-class object in the capacity data layer so every downstream tool sees in-flight capacity, not only what has landed. Run a portfolio of bring-ups in parallel — new cloud regions, on-prem sites, neocloud blocks — with one integrated schedule spanning provider milestones, cluster creation, network turn-up, storage readiness, health burn-in, and first-workload landing. Drive readiness automation: All capacity systems are fully integrated for all new capacity, from contracted through ingested, automated and scaled. Instrument and publish the numbers that matter — time-to-occupied and paid-idle dollars per tranche — with executive-level reporting on status, tradeoffs, and risk across the portfolio. What you bring Significant experience delivering large-scale infrastructure — cloud regions, accelerator clusters, HPC systems, or bare-metal fleets — at multi-region scale or ≥10k accelerators (or CPU/storage equivalent). Technical range from through cluster orchestration and node health, up to the telemetry and planning tables on top — enough to debug where they disagree rather than route it. SQL and enough Python to answer your own questions and build your own reporting. A degree in a technical field or an equivalent engineering track record. Preferred Reserved-capacity onboarding, private offers, or capacity commitments with cloud or neocloud providers. Enough demand-planning exposure to challenge a forecast, translate it into per-tranche requirements, and feed delivery variance back into it. Data center or colocation delivery: power and space planning, network turn-up, site acceptance, vendor management. Accelerator health and burn-in, collective-communications sanity testing, or fleet-health SLOs — and a rigorous definition of "healthy." Systems of record or lifecycle services for infrastructure assets. Onboarding a new hardware generation into an existing scheduler and observability stack. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.Annual Salary:$320,000—$405,000 USDLogistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

rows.description:
LilEngine is leading the Lakehouse, a company-strategic effort to make Apache Iceberg a first-class citizen in Spotify's data ecosystem. We're building it in close collaboration with Google, on open standards, so that different kinds of data are queryable the same way and teams can bring the right engine, from BigQuery to Dataflow to Trino, to the job.
The work has two parts. Hecate enables Iceberg for the Parquet datasets that already exist across Spotify, so teams get the benefits without rewriting their data. Alongside it, we're building the foundations of a new Lakehouse architecture that lets workflows write Iceberg tables natively. We're shipping the MVP this cycle, and you'll help shape what comes next.
We also own BigQuery for all of Spotify. Thousands of engineers, data scientists and pipelines depend on it every day, which puts us on the critical path for storing, finding and querying data. We're judged on reliability, cost efficiency and how quickly we unblock users when something breaks. This backend role sits where open table formats, cloud data warehouses and processing engines meet.

What You'll Do:
Build and evolve the lakehouse: Help build the foundations that let data workflows read and write Iceberg tables directly, from this cycle's MVP to a production-grade platform. Drive adoption: Help migrate data pipelines from across Spotify onto the new stack, making the move as painless as possible through tooling, standards and hands-on support. raw_data.descriptionPlain:
LilEngine is leading the Lakehouse, a company-strategic effort to make Apache Iceberg a first-class citizen in Spotify's data ecosystem. We're building it in close collaboration with Google, on open standards, so that different kinds of data are queryable the same way and teams can bring the right engine, from BigQuery to Dataflow to Trino, to the job.
The work has two parts. Hecate enables Iceberg for the Parquet datasets that already exist across Spotify, so teams get the benefits without rewriting their data. Alongside it, we're building the foundations of a new Lakehouse architecture that lets workflows write Iceberg tables natively. We're shipping the MVP this cycle, and you'll help shape what comes next.
We also own BigQuery for all of Spotify. Thousands of engineers, data scientists and pipelines depend on it every day, which puts us on the critical path for storing, finding and querying data. We're judged on reliability, cost efficiency and how quickly we unblock users when something breaks. This backend role sits where open table formats, cloud data warehouses and processing engines meet.

Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.An overview of this role As Lead Legal Counsel, Corporate, you'll own securities, public company reporting, and corporate governance work for GitLab, a growing public technology company. You'll join the Legal & Corporate Affairs (LACA) team as a senior individual contributor, reporting to the Senior Director, Associate General Counsel, Corporate & Compliance. You'll bring a strong securities law foundation and a broad corporate perspective to a small team. Your work will span quarterly reporting and earnings, the annual proxy statement and stockholders meeting, board and committee matters, equity plans, and subsidiary governance. You'll also support mergers and acquisitions (M&A) and other strategic initiatives. You'll work closely with Accounting, Corporate Development, Finance, Investor Relations, People, Product, Stock Administration, Tax, and Treasury. You'll translate complex legal issues into clear recommendations, build trust across functions, and balance legal risk with business objectives. What You’ll Do Own securities and public company reporting matters, working with internal stakeholders and external auditors on Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings, quarterly reports, earnings releases, the annual proxy statement, investor presentations, and other public disclosures. Advise on corporate governance, including board and committee processes, the annual stockholders meeting, corporate approvals, equity plan matters, executive compensation, and related compliance requirements. Provide legal guidance on complex entity matters across jurisdictions, including formation, maintenance, reorganizations, intercompany agreements, and wind-downs. Support M&A and other strategic transactions, contributing to diligence, documentation, approvals, signing, closing, and post-closing integration. Engage and manage outside counsel across jurisdictions, coordinating work and ensuring practical, high-quality, and cost-effective advice. Identify legal and business risks, present clear options to senior stakeholders, and monitor legal developments to keep policies, processes, and controls current. Build and improve playbooks, checklists, templates, and workflows for recurring corporate legal work. Train junior legal team members and cross-functional partners to use these resources. What You’ll Bring 6+ years of demonstrated relevant legal experience, including law firm experience advising US-listed public companies on securities law, corporate governance, and public company reporting. Prior in-house experience is a plus. A Juris Doctor (JD) degree and active admission to a US state bar. The ability to independently manage complex legal matters and cross-functional projects, prioritize competing needs, and drive work to completion with limited direction. Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical legal issues to non-lawyers and senior leaders and build trusted working relationships. The ability to investigate unfamiliar legal questions, weigh risks against business objectives, and turn recommendations into action. Experience improving legal processes, templates, policies, or other scalable resources. The ability to collaborate in a remote, globally distributed team across time zones and cultures, and willingness to use GitLab in your day-to-day work. Helpful but not required: in-house work at a public software-as-a-service (SaaS), software, or open core company; M&A; cross-border corporate matters; outside counsel management; or legal technology that helps scale legal work. About the team The Corporate & Compliance team supports principled corporate governance and GitLab's culture of compliance. We work with leaders and subject matter experts across LACA and the broader company to provide practical, timely legal guidance. LACA is a globally distributed team that supports GitLab's growth through legal expertise, business partnership, and continuous process improvement. We work transparently, collaborate across functions and time zones, and use GitLab's own tools and AI-enabled workflows to make legal support more efficient and accessible. rows.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.About the role Anthropic's customer-facing teams are often the first place a customer sees what Claude can do. As a Demo Engineer, you'll build the demos, reference implementations, and reusable tooling that help those teams make new capabilities tangible, relevant, and trustworthy, ideally within days of a product launch rather than weeks after. This role sits between product engineering, technical storytelling, and GTM execution. You'll own ambiguous, high-leverage problems end to end: prototyping an agentic experience for a new capability, then hardening it into something reliable that other teams can run on their own. You'll work closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Operations, and our sales and solutions teams, and you'll bring what you learn from customer-facing work back to the people building the products. Because a demo is frequently someone's first impression of what our models can and can't do, accuracy and honesty matter as much as polish. Success in this role looks like customer-facing teams demonstrating new capabilities sooner and with more confidence, recurring requests becoming reusable assets rather than one-off projects, and field insights shaping product and launch-readiness decisions. Responsibilities Own demo readiness for new and priority Claude capabilities, including environments, integrations, synthetic data, evaluations, reliability checks, and fallback paths Build prototypes, agents, and reference flows that make complex capabilities concrete and tie them to clear customer outcomes Turn recurring requests into reusable accelerators such as companion apps, templates, Skills, plugins, and self-service demo packages that scale across customer-facing teams Partner with GTM colleagues on high-impact customer moments, unblock critical technical gaps, and spot the patterns worth turning into shared assets Build internal agentic systems that automate demo preparation, validation, and asset maintenance, so demos stay current as products change Translate patterns from customer-facing work into product feedback, launch-readiness priorities, and systemic improvements with Product and Engineering Define and raise the bar for demo quality across accuracy, safety, reliability, usability, and adoption Decide when a customer need calls for a bespoke build and when it should become a shared capability You may be a good fit if you have Proficiency in Python or TypeScript, with experience shipping working software end to end Hands-on experience building applications or agents on top of LLM APIs, including prompting, tool use, and retrieval Experience designing integrations with third-party APIs, data sources, and services The ability to take an ambiguous capability or customer need to a working prototype quickly, and then make it reliable Clear communication of technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences, including sales and solutions teams Comfort collaborating across Product, Engineering, Marketing, Operations, and GTM teams Experience in a demo engineering, solutions engineering, sales engineering, forward deployed engineering, developer relations, or product engineering role A track record of building reusable internal tools, templates, or self-service assets that other teams adopted Hands-on experience with Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK, the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Skills, or plugins Experience building evaluation or validation harnesses for AI systems, including reliability checks and graceful fallbacks Experience building always-on or scheduled agentic systems that automate internal workflows Experience building synthetic or sanitized datasets that make demos realistic without exposing sensitive information Front-end or product design skills that help demos feel polished and intuitive Experience supporting product launches or running launch-readiness programs A history of turning field feedback into concrete product input that influenced a roadmap A passion for making powerful technology safe and beneficial, and a commitment to representing model capabilities accurately and honestly The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.Annual Salary:$240,000—$315,000 USDLogistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

rows.description:
You’ll join the Premium Growth India team within the Markets & Subscriptions organisation, focused on making Spotify Premium an increasingly desirable music experience in India. Sitting at the intersection of marketing, product, music, and strategy, the team works closely with Music, Marketing, Partnerships, and other teams to grow Premium through cultural relevance and artist-led initiatives. In this role, you’ll own Premium desirability and the artist and partner Premium flywheel for India, shaping how we work with artists, cultural moments, fandom, and partnerships to drive Premium consideration and measurable conversion at scale.

What You’ll Do:
Define and execute the Premium desirability strategy for India, using artist-led and culturally relevant initiatives to drive consideration and conversion. Own the artist and partner flywheel for Premium growth, evolving artist advocacy, fan experiences, and partnership programs toward measurable Premium outcomes. Shape and execute the Premium opportunity within existing in-person activations, including film partnerships, bespoke music events, festivals, and other relevant cultural moments. Partner with local Music & Podcasts, Marketing, Partnerships, and other teams to identify and activate artists, creators, and partners that can help grow Premium. Design and run desirability initiatives with clear success metrics, using performance data and audience behaviour to understand what works and continuously improve the strategy. Own the fandom value opportunity for Premium end-to-end, from identifying opportunities to partnering with Product on fan-facing Premium features and experiences. Develop business cases and evaluate the impact of desirability, artist, and partner initiatives to inform where we invest and scale. Capture and share learnings that strengthen the India Premium Growth playbook, contribute to cross-regional Growth initiatives, and support adjacent growth priorities when business needs require it. Integrate AI-driven tools and workflows thoughtfully to improve decision-making and execution efficiency.

Who You Are:
You have 5+ years of experience across growth, marketing, partnerships, strategy, or related roles in a digital consumer business such as streaming, music, entertainment, media, or technology. You have strong experience with music and fandom and understand how fan communities form, what drives engagement, and how fandom can translate into measurable business outcomes. You understand growth marketing and connect cultural and creative ideas to measurable outcomes such as consideration, conversion, and subscriber growth. You have experience independently owning and scaling artist-led campaigns, partnerships, live experiences, or similarly complex consumer initiatives from strategy through execution and measurement. You are comfortable using data and audience insights to make decisions, test hypotheses, measure impact, and refine your approach. You work effectively across functions and can influence outcomes without direct authority, particularly when collaborating with Music, Marketing, Partnerships, Product, and other teams. You are curious about cultural trends and user behaviour in India and enjoy testing, learning, and iterating to understand what drives Premium consideration and conversion. Experience working directly with artists, labels, fan platforms, music or entertainment marketing, or Product teams on consumer-facing experiences can help you succeed in this role.

Where You’ll Be:
This role is based in Mumbai We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

rows.description:
The Audiobooks Mission is a team in the Product & Technology organisation focused on the ecosystem and strategies of Audiobooks on Spotify. We work across both the creator and consumer audiobooks ecosystems, in order to get the best possible product to market with the best possible content.
Spotify's Audiobooks team is helping shape the future of audio storytelling by bringing the world's best audiobook experiences to millions of listeners. As Associate Manager, Audiobook Licensing & Author Partnerships, you'll play an important role in growing our catalog while building meaningful relationships across the independent publishing community.
You'll work with entrepreneurial authors, hybrid publishers, independent presses, and distribution partners to identify great content, negotiate commercial partnerships, and help creators succeed on Spotify. Working closely with cross-functional teams across Product, Editorial, Growth, Operations, and Finance, you'll help scale our audiobook business while creating exceptional experiences for both creators and listeners.

What You'll Do:
Identify and evaluate audiobook catalogs from independent authors, hybrid publishers, independent presses, and distribution partners that will resonate with Spotify listeners. Negotiate audiobook licensing agreements and commercial partnerships that create long-term value for Spotify and our publishing partners. Build trusted relationships across a diverse portfolio of independent publishers, distributors, and authors, serving as their primary strategic contact. Develop creative partnership structures that support sustainable growth while meeting the evolving needs of creators and publishing businesses. Use market insights, performance analytics, and commercial data to inform acquisition strategies and identify new partnership opportunities. Partner with creators and publishers to optimize catalog performance, improve discoverability, and resolve operational challenges. Collaborate closely with Product, Editorial, Growth, Operations, Finance, and other cross-functional teams to improve partner experience and support Spotify's audiobook strategy. Advocate internally for the needs of independent creators and publishers, helping shape future product capabilities and strategic initiatives. Contribute to initiatives focused on catalog expansion, subscriber value, listening growth, operational excellence, and blended cost per content hour (CPCH) optimization.

Who You Are:
You have 3+ years of experience in publishing, digital media, business development, content licensing, content partnerships, or a related field. You have experience negotiating and closing commercial licensing, distribution, or partnership agreements. You have a strong understanding of the independent publishing ecosystem, including indie authors, hybrid publishers, audiobook distributors, and digital publishing models. You understand the unique opportunities and challenges facing entrepreneurial creators and independent publishing businesses. You build trusted relationships and effectively influence a broad range of internal and external stakeholders. You use data, financial insights, and market trends to inform commercial decisions and partnership strategies. You manage multiple priorities effectively while maintaining strong attention to detail in a fast-paced environment. You are comfortable navigating ambiguity, taking ownership, and finding practical solutions to complex business challenges. You care about helping creators succeed and are passionate about audiobooks, storytelling, and the evolving creator economy. You hold a Bachelor's degree; an MBA or other advanced degree is beneficial. You are comfortable collaborating across multiple time zones and are willing to travel when needed.

Where You'll Be:
We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! For this role, you can be within the North Americas region as long as we have a work location.

The United States base range for this position is $74,000 – $106,000 USD, plus equity. The benefits available for this position include health insurance, six-month paid parental leave, 401(k) retirement plan, monthly meal allowance, 23 paid days off, paid flexible holidays, and paid sick leave. These ranges may be modified in the future.


Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.
 
At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

Spotify is looking for a short-term contractor for the Artist & Label Partnerships team in Vietnam. 
The Artist & Label Partnerships team are the face of Spotify to artists, managers, labels & distributors. Focusing on the Vietnamese music landscape, this role will serve as the point of contact for record labels, distributors and artists, ensuring that artists & their teams are familiar with Spotify standard methodologies, resources and tools. The role will closely support the cross-functional teams with on-platform promotion and off-platform artist marketing. 

Please note this is a fixed-term, 6 months, contractor role hired through a third party.

What You'll Do:
Maintain positive partnerships across artist and label communities within Vietnam. Support our key partners in Vietnam on Spotify tools, resources and insights. Work closely with our cross functional teams to support artists and labels on priority releases in Vietnam Collaborate with the regional Music team to ensure content strategies are localized and successfully executed. Ensure Spotify has the best possible content offering in Vietnam and use this to further Spotify’s appeal to existing and new users.

Who You Are:
You have at least 3+ years of working experience in the music/entertainment industry. Regional and global experience would be an added advantage.  Extremely well organized, dedicated with the ability to plan, deliver on tight deadlines and pay outstanding attention to detail. You have a deep understanding and established network within the local music industry in Vietnam and have built relevant contacts with labels and artists to effectively collaborate with the community. You have a strong background in music and technology and a consistent record with operations. You have a strong grasp of content knowledge, music and cultural trends, artists, user engagement and behaviors.  You have excellent stakeholder management skills.  You have experience working within Vietnam and ideally across multiple markets within regional and global teams. You are very fluent in written and spoken English and Vietnamese.  And finally, a great teammate, adapt well to change, and always have a positive demeanor.

Where You'll Be:
This contract is based in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

rows.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.About the role We're looking for a Commercial Counsel, SPARC (Safety, Policy, and Research Contracts) to join our legal team at the forefront of shaping how cutting-edge AI technology reaches users, researchers, and enterprises worldwide. You'll work alongside experienced colleagues who operate as true strategic partners—moving fast, thinking creatively, and working collaboratively on cutting-edge AI safety and research agreements, including threat-sharing frameworks with leading security organizations and collaborations that shape and advance responsible AI development standards. This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated attorney to develop deep expertise in their commercial transactions career while contributing directly to responsible AI development. Key responsibilities Draft, review, and negotiate commercial agreements, focusing mainly on AI safety and research agreements, as well as product and strategic partnership agreements Partner closely with beneficial deployments, health, policy, and education partnerships teams to support deal velocity and provide practical legal guidance Draft program terms for the phased deployment of AI models with frontier capabilities in cybersecurity and health sciences. Help build and maintain commercial legal infrastructure, including contract templates, playbooks, and process improvements Partner with Policy, Safeguards, and Research teams on novel AI governance initiatives Identify and escalate legal risks appropriately while supporting business momentum Stay current on legal developments affecting AI technologies Minimum qualifications Hold a law degree (JD, LLB, or equivalent) and meet the local licensing requirements to work as in house counsel where you’ll be based Experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating commercial agreements Demonstrated ability to provide clear, practical legal guidance to non-lawyers on complex commercial law matters Preferred qualifications Commercial experience supporting research collaborations and sponsored research and grant giving programs Curiosity about AI technology and AI policy, and a commitment to responsible AI developmentExperience with biotech, clinical research, or other life sciences transactions Familiarity with grant-making or grant-funded arrangements, including funding terms and compliance considerations Experience advising on partnerships with non-profit foundations, academic institutions, or industry trade groups Comfort advising research teams whose work doesn't follow a standard commercial playbook Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate legal concepts for non-legal audiences A collaborative approach to working with colleagues and external partners Experience navigating multi-stakeholder agreements involving technical and policy considerations Ability to adapt to shifting priorities in a fast-paced environment Experience with SaaS agreements or other technology transactions The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.Annual Salary:$265,000—$335,000 USDLogistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. rows.role: Senior Digital Learning Experience Designer - Learning & Inclusion
rows.description:
We’re looking for a Senior Digital Learning Experience Designer to join our Learning & Inclusion team, the group responsible for creating learning experiences that help every Spotify band member grow, belong, and do their best work.
You’ll bring together instructional design, visual design, storytelling, and broader learning and development expertise to create inclusive and effective experiences at scale. You’ll partner with subject-matter experts, people leaders, and Learning & Inclusion colleagues on company-wide initiatives, from leadership development to programs that bring Spotify’s values to life.

What You'll Do:
Lead the end-to-end design of learning experiences, from needs analysis and curriculum architecture through development, launch, and evaluation. Partner with subject-matter experts and stakeholders to identify performance needs and turn them into clear learning objectives and practical solutions. Design learning journeys across live, digital, blended, and self-directed formats using evidence-based learning principles. Create engaging learning materials, including eLearning, facilitator guides, participant resources, job aids, presentations, and micro-learning experiences. Use visual design and storytelling to make complex ideas clear, memorable, and engaging while creating experiences that feel unmistakably Spotify. Build interactive digital learning experiences using AI-assisted workflows and authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline or Rise, Adobe Captivate, or similar platforms. Design inclusive learning experiences that reflect different perspectives, reduce barriers to participation, and support a culture of belonging. Pilot and iterate on learning experiences using learner feedback, stakeholder input, and performance data. Define meaningful measures of success and evaluate learning effectiveness, knowledge transfer, learner experience, and behavior change. Manage multiple learning projects from initial scoping through delivery while creating clarity around priorities, timelines, and stakeholder expectations. Explore emerging approaches in learning design, including AI-assisted authoring and adaptive learning, and apply them where they can meaningfully improve the learner experience.

Who You Are:
You have 5+ years of professional instructional design experience and a portfolio demonstrating thoughtful work across multiple learning formats. You apply learning science principles such as cognitive load, retrieval practice, spaced learning, and adult learning theory to practical design decisions. You know how to uncover learning and performance needs, translate them into measurable objectives, and design learning journeys that build knowledge and skills over time. You create meaningful practice through scenarios, simulations, assessments, and other interactive experiences rather than relying on passive content. You have strong visual and UX design judgment and understand how typography, hierarchy, layout, and visual storytelling can make learning clearer and easier to navigate. You have experience with rapid authoring tools such as Articulate 360, Captivate, Lectora, or similar platforms, along with design tools such as Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, or equivalent. You can create clear storyboards, scripts, facilitator guides, and supporting materials that help others confidently deliver consistent learning experiences. You use learner feedback and data to evaluate effectiveness, iterate on your work, and connect learning experiences to meaningful outcomes. You communicate complex ideas clearly and collaborate effectively with subject-matter experts, leaders, and cross-functional partners. You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity, balancing multiple priorities, and taking ownership from an early idea through a polished learning experience. You bring experience in areas such as inclusive learning design, leadership development, learning technology, short-form learning video or animation, LMS/LXP platforms, or SCORM/xAPI. You have a degree in instructional design, learning sciences, education, human-computer interaction, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in New York We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

The United States base range for this position is $87,000 – $125,000 USD, plus equity. The benefits available for this position include health insurance, six-month paid parental leave, 401(k) retirement plan, monthly meal allowance, 23 paid days off, paid flexible holidays, and paid sick leave. These ranges may be modified in the future.


Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.
 
At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

rows.description:
We’re the Markets & Subscribers business unit, a truly cross-functional team focused on finding future listeners, wherever and whoever they may be. We work collaboratively, combining marketing, insights, product development, design, and engineering expertise to grow Spotify’s subscribers and monthly active users in both new and existing markets across the globe. Join us and you’ll be part of a dynamic team taking acquisition, activation, and business growth at Spotify to the next level.
 Spotify is looking for a Performance Marketing Activation Specialist to join the band and help drive direct response marketing efforts. You'll be part of the in-house Performance Marketing team - planning, launching, and optimizing global acquisition and conversion campaigns across paid search and paid social, owning every part of the campaign process. You'll work closely with cross-functional partners, analytics teams, and external platforms and agencies to deliver results. A desire to learn more about data and tech innovation is a must have for future growth in the role.

What You'll Do:
Own daily campaign stewardship (trafficking, QA, launch, high-touch optimization, reporting) with a primary focus on Google Search campaigns. Additional channels include, but are not limited to: Paid Social (Meta, Snapchat, TikTok), Google App Campaigns (ACi, ACe), Apple Search Ads (ASA) Contribute to campaign strategy and budget recommendations for large-scale, multi-million dollar direct response initiatives (app install and web conversion), managing pacing and billing reconciliation. Design and run A/B tests and experiments, analyze results against the learning agenda, and deliver concise reporting in partnership with analytics. Support incrementality testing, partnering with internal and platform analytics teams, across both Conversion Lift and GeoX methodologies.  Partner with the broader Strategy team to optimize across channels, including coordinating Search and Social strategies. Cultivating and maintaining vendor and platform relationships and maximizing their potential

Who You Are:
3+ years of hands-on performance marketing execution experience running app install and/or web conversion campaigns; in-house experience a plus. Deep hands-on experience managing Google Brand and Nonbrand Search campaigns; experience with other native platforms (Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, Google App, Apple Search) and optimization tools (Smartly) a plus.  Data oriented with strong Excel/Sheets skills that you can turn into clear stories and presentations for stakeholders with varying levels of digital expertise. Knowledge of the Marketing Technology ecosystem and the role each piece plays in attributing media performance; familiarity with MMPs, website pixels, CDPs, Google Analytics, Tableau, etc. Experience using AI tools to streamline day-to-day work, especially to automate campaign trafficking and management. Detail-oriented, analytical, and results-driven, with excellent communication skills and a pulse on where digital advertising is heading. Educated to BA/BS level or have equivalent experience. Self-motivated and thrive in a fast-paced environment, executing independently, navigating complexity, and building judgment through doing. Good character and a strong work ethic; your contributions raise the quality and dependability of the team's output and you address issues before they escalate. Curious and open-minded; you do your best work in collaborative teams, sharing context proactively, seeking guidance when needed, and engaging constructively when team direction conflicts with data.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in New York. We offer flexibility to work where you work best, with 2–3 days per week in the office. Collaboration hours align to the EST time zone.

The United States base range for this position is $73,000 – $104,000 USD, plus equity. The benefits available for this position include health insurance, six-month paid parental leave, 401(k) retirement plan, monthly meal allowance, 23 paid days off, paid flexible holidays, and paid sick leave. These ranges may be modified in the future.

So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.
 
At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. rows.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.About the role Anthropic is building AI systems that will shape the trajectory of one of the most consequential technologies in human history. That work requires physical infrastructure at significant scale, and building that infrastructure the right way means being a real, long-term partner to the communities where we operate. We are looking for a Community Engagement Manager in Montana and Utah to join our Public Policy team and serve as Anthropic's on-the-ground presence in the communities where our data centers are sited, built, and operated. This is not a communications role or a government affairs role, though you will do elements of both. It is a relationship role: your job is to make Anthropic a trusted, visible, and valued neighbor, from the earliest stages of site selection through construction and long-term operations. You will be the connective tissue between Anthropic's Policy and Infrastructure teams and the local officials, community organizations, economic development partners, and residents who have a stake in what we build. You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly. Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand. You will travel regularly within Montana and Utah, up to 50% of the time, often over long distances, and occasionally to other Anthropic data center markets. Key responsibilities Build and maintain trusted, sustained relationships with county commissioners, mayors and city and town councils, planning and zoning bodies, state economic development agencies (such as Montana's Department of Commerce and Utah's Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity), community groups, civic leaders, educational institutions, and workforce partners in the Montana and Utah data center markets you cover Engage respectfully and meaningfully with Tribal governments and Native communities in Montana and Utah, recognizing Tribal sovereignty, building sustained relationships, and supporting consultation and partnership efforts related to our projects Develop and execute a community engagement strategy for each of your markets, spanning site selection, rows.description:
The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we're behind some of Spotify's most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you'll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.

Within Personalization, the Speak Team owns the development of Spotify's state-of-the-art speech models, contributing to speech recognition, speech synthesis, and speech-to-speech models. We craft voice models that match human-level emotional expressiveness, so we can deeply engage our listeners and support creators at scale. Our groundbreaking work on speech synthesis relies on state-of-the-art deep learning methods and evaluation techniques, highly efficient data processing and model serving, and capturing audio of outstanding quality from our voice talent pool.

We're looking for a senior applied research scientist with experience in developing novel ML techniques and architectures and with a strong interest in working across a full production pipeline to produce state-of-the-art generative conversational speech-to-speech models. You'll collaborate with our engineering teams to help develop our production pipelines, explore new ideas and methods to improve quality, understanding and realism, as well as push the frontiers of what is possible with our speech technology.

What You'll Do:
Develop and experiment with new methods for speech synthesis and speech recognition, along with end-to-end approaches, building on the latest research and ideas. Work towards the expansion of our speech use-cases targeting different markets and products. Be part of a highly motivated research team dedicated to building and creating models at scale to power the Spotify platform. Champion best practices for research and development, sharing your knowledge and experience with other researchers within Speak. Collaborate with our engineering and data teams on ideas requiring new infrastructure or new high-quality data, as well as to help improve our speech recognition and speech synthesis pipelines, and help turn proven ideas into scalable products.

Who You Are:
You have a strong background in ML (PhD degree on top of professional experience), and experience in working with any of the following: transformers, GANs, diffusion models, flow matching, VAEs, audio codecs. You have experience in developing generative models for speech synthesis, speech recognition, audio/music, natural language processing, or computer vision. You have strong experience with Python, particularly PyTorch. You have strong communication skills and the ability to explain technical ideas with clarity to technical and non-technical people alike. You have experience in an academic or professional setting conducting high-quality research.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in New York City. We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home

The United States base range for this position is $169,157 - $241,653 plus equity. The benefits available for this position include health insurance, six month paid parental leave, 401(k) retirement plan, a monthly meal allowance, 23 paid days off, 13 paid flexible holidays. These ranges may be modified in the future.


Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.
 
At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.
