rows.description:
We design Spotify’s consumer experience—end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening and watching feel effortless, personal, and joyful for hundreds of millions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify.
We’re seeking a Principal Product Manager to help lead the consumer experience across Spotify’s formats, including books, podcasts, and music. Format Foundations partners with the business teams behind each format to lead innovation in how users discover, engage with, and build lasting relationships with content on Spotify. You’ll set the product vision and strategy for your area and shape feature portfolios across formats. This role sits within Format Foundations in Core Experience, partnering closely with these teams to grow their businesses through product innovation.

What You'll Do:
Lead product vision and strategy across Spotify’s formats, shaping how books, podcasts, and music become more engaging, lovable, and valuable for users, creators, and the business. Define and evolve the user experience across the content journey—from discovery and evaluation through engagement, library management, and retention. Partner closely with business leaders across books, podcasts, and music to translate business strategy into product innovation that drives growth. Drive innovation across multimodal and cross-format experiences, such as the intersection of listening and reading, and build capabilities that can scale from one format to others. Work closely with engineering, design, data, and cross-functional partners to deliver high-quality experiences. Use data, experimentation, and user insights to inform decisions and continuously improve the experience. Align senior stakeholders across Core Experience, the business teams, and Personalization to create a cohesive consumer experience. Lead multiple cross-functional initiatives end to end, owning scope and alignment and partnering with engineering on delivery. Mentor product managers and raise the bar for product craft across the team.

Who You Are:
You have 10+ years of experience in product management and have led product work across several consumer media products at scale in large technology companies. You have deep knowledge of the consumer media landscape across areas such as books, podcasts, or music, including competitive dynamics, creator and publisher ecosystems, and user behavior. You have experience building for mobile platforms such as iOS and Android, including complex user interfaces. You understand how to build scalable systems and experiences that enable teams to move faster. You’re able to balance user experience, technical constraints, and business impact. You care deeply about creating intuitive, high-quality consumer experiences. You’ve worked closely with engineering, design, and data partners to bring products to life. You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity and bringing clarity across teams and organizations. You’ve influenced senior leaders and stakeholders across functions and levels to drive alignment and outcomes. You actively use AI tools in your product development workflow, from research and analysis to iteration and prototyping.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in Stockholm or London We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

rows.description:
Content Platform is responsible for ingesting, processing, storing, and delivering every piece of content on Spotify — from music and podcasts to audiobooks. Within Content Platform, the Media domain owns the end-to-end media pipeline, from the moment content arrives through to seamless playback for listeners around the world. We're looking for a Staff Engineer to provide architectural leadership across this media platform. You’ll help shape and drive the technical direction from ingestion through transcoding, packaging, storage, delivery, and playback. This is a role for someone who thinks in systems, understands the trade-offs between codec choices and infrastructure costs, and can drive technical strategy across multiple teams at scale.

What You'll Do:
Define and drive the long-term architectural direction for Spotify's media pipeline across Content Platform. Lead large-scale technical initiatives that span multiple squads and organizations, including projects such as media delivery, codec rollouts, and future playback capabilities. Partner closely with engineering managers, product managers, and senior engineers to align technical strategy with product priorities, reliability goals, and cost efficiency, acting as a key technical counterpart for media architecture. Guide architectural decisions across media ingestion, transcoding, packaging, storage, content delivery, and playback. Author and review RFCs, architecture decision records, and technical design documents that guide engineering teams and leadership. Mentor senior engineers across the organization, helping raise technical quality, architectural thinking, and engineering excellence. Bring a cost-aware engineering mindset by understanding how media architecture decisions impact compute, storage, CDN utilization, and long-term platform sustainability.

Who You Are:
You have deep expertise building large-scale media platforms spanning audio, video, encoding, transcoding, packaging, delivery, and playback technologies. You have successfully led architecture across multiple engineering teams and influenced technical direction beyond your immediate organization. You have significant experience designing and operating distributed systems at internet scale, including high-throughput media processing, large-scale storage, and globally distributed delivery infrastructure. You understand the architectural trade-offs between codecs, packaging formats, playback technologies, storage, networking, and infrastructure costs. You have a strong track record of leading multi-quarter technical initiatives from initial proposal through implementation and organization-wide adoption. You communicate technical ideas clearly through well-structured RFCs, design documents, and architectural decision records. You build trust through collaboration and technical credibility, bringing together teams with different priorities to deliver shared outcomes. You enjoy mentoring experienced engineers and helping organizations grow their technical capability. Experience working with cloud infrastructure providers, CDN vendors, and large-scale media delivery ecosystems is highly valued.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in London or Stockholm We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

  • Partner closely with engineering managers, product managers, and senior engineers to align technical strategy with product priorities, reliability goals, and cost efficiency, acting as a key technical counterpart for media architecture.
  • Guide architectural decisions across media ingestion, transcoding, packaging, storage, content delivery, and playback.
  • Author and review RFCs, architecture decision records, and technical design documents that guide engineering teams and leadership.

• You have deep expertise building large-scale media platforms spanning audio, video, encoding, transcoding, packaging, delivery, and playback technologies.
  • You have successfully led architecture across multiple engineering teams and influenced technical direction beyond your immediate organization.
  • You have significant experience designing and operating distributed systems at internet scale, including high-throughput media processing, large-scale storage, and globally distributed delivery infrastructure.

rows.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.About the role As a Capacity Deployment Lead within Anthropic's Data Center Operations (DCO) organization, you will support and scale how we bring new compute capacity online across a growing fleet of partner-operated data centers. Deployment runs from construction kickoff to ready for service (RFS). You are engaged during planning and construction, and on-site and hands-on from EFA through infrastructure delivery and receiving, integration QA, power-on and network turn-up, burn-in and validation, and acceptance. You work with hardware vendors and operations partners for completion of each CU (capacity unit) with a structured handover into production operations and the maintenance program. The scope is compute: accelerator systems, racks, and the infrastructure around them - at the sites in service today and the ones coming online behind them. This is a program and execution role. You will work with the Global Capacity Delivery Program Lead and the broader Data Center Operations organization, to extend its coverage across more sites and platforms as the fleet grows. Expect 50%+ travel: you get eyes on via boots-on-the-ground for each site in preparation for and during delivery, deployment, QA, and close-out, and your authority comes from being there. Working with vendors and partners, you set direction, priorities, and standards for execution, and you prove results with Anthropic-owned data rather than self-reported status. What you learn at one site - what worked, what slipped, what should become standard - becomes the playbook for the next wave. If you have delivered data center hardware at scale, are passionate about HPC data centers, & enjoy working in complex, fast-paced environments, we welcome you to apply. Responsibilities Include: Own deployment outcomes for your assigned sites and data-hall waves: CUs and hall ready-for-service dates met, with exceptions closed out, or risk called early enough for leadership to act. Engage from construction kickoff and confirm deployment readiness ahead of each wave - floor access, power, network, receiving paths, and partner staffing - working the gaps with the site operations partner and facilities counterparts before racks arrive. Be on site at key points before and during delivery, deployment, QA, and close-out; verify the work with your own eyes rather than from a dashboard, and support the on-site teams with your direct expertise. Work with partner's site leadership to ensure success through rack delivery and receiving, integration QA, power-on and network turn-up, and burn-in and validation, setting daily priorities and quality gates and confirming results against Anthropic-owned ticket and telemetry data. Validate the handover gate for each CU and data hall: acceptance criteria met, burn-in complete, documentation delivered, spares positioned, ticketing live, and a structured handover into production operations and the maintenance program. Turn best practices, optimization, and lessons learned from each deployment into program-wide improvements: procedures, checklists, acceptance standards, and metrics, so the next wave runs faster and cleaner than the last. Extend the deployment program to new sites and platforms, adapting standards and acceptance criteria as the hardware changes. Communicate deployment status, dependencies, constraints, and risk to engineering, capacity planning, the team that owns the overall site schedule, and leadership. You may be a good fit if you: Have 8+ years of experience in data center operations or hardware deployment as a manager, technical lead or related role, including accountability for delivery milestones. Can demonstrate a proven track record leading compute or network hardware deployments at a large scale across multiple sites or data-hall waves, from early floor access through ready for service. Have managed vendors, OEMs, or contract workforces to measurable outcomes: milestones, quality gates, operational reviews, and corrective action. Possess hands-on technical depth in server, network, and rack-level hardware, enough to independently verify deployment quality and audit vendor claims. Have built or substantially improved operational processes. Are comfortable working with schedule, ticket, and telemetry data to drive decisions. Can travel heavily and work on site for extended stretches, including during delivery surges and turn-up windows. 50% Travel expected. Possess a bachelor's degree in relevant domain or equivalent practical experience. It’s a bonus if you have: Experience with GPU/accelerator or high-density liquid-cooled infrastructure, including bring-up of liquid-cooled racks. Experience standing up operations at a new site or data hall, from commissioning handoff through first deployment. Experience deploying more than one accelerator platform, or introducing a new hardware platform into an existing deployment program. Experience delivering deployment outcomes inside partner-operated or colocation sites where on-the-floor operations are staffed via third parties. Familiarity with dense accelerator network cabling, optics, and high-speed interconnect at rack and pod scale. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.Annual Salary:$320,000—$405,000 USDLogistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

rows.description:
The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

User Platform builds the identity and access capabilities that help people use Spotify safely and easily. We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager to shape how people access Spotify and stay connected across our apps, devices, and strategic partner integrations. You’ll focus on session management - how Spotify recognizes someone after they sign in, maintains their access, and enables them to connect or disconnect devices and applications.

You’ll bring together consumer experience and technical product strategy, working closely with engineering, design, research, insights, security, and teams responsible for Spotify’s clients and partnerships. Your decisions will help people get to the experiences they want, stay in control of their access, and use Spotify with confidence.

What You'll Do:
Define the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for session management across Spotify’s clients, device types, and strategic partner integrations. Use research, data, and feedback from users and developers to identify access friction and prioritize improvements with the greatest potential impact. Improve how sessions are established, maintained, and ended, balancing reliable access with account protection, privacy, and user control. Shape device connection, session transfer, and partner authorization experiences, including clear consent when an app requests access or additional capabilities. Partner with engineering to make session and access capabilities reusable and easier to adopt through APIs, client components, documentation, and clear integration guidance. Work across client, device, and partner teams to understand different needs, align priorities, and carry improvements through delivery and adoption. Define success measures for access quality, user friction, developer experience, and adoption, connecting those measures to meaningful user and business outcomes. Make thoughtful trade-offs between immediate experience improvements, long-term technical investment, security, and privacy while providing teams with clear direction and context.

Who You Are:
You have several years of product management experience and can demonstrate how products you’ve shipped improved outcomes for users or developers. You have experience working on consumer products, identity and access, connected devices, developer products, or partner integrations. You understand how technical capabilities such as session management, authorization, APIs, client behavior, or consent flows can shape the end-user and developer experience. You have strong product and user experience judgment and enjoy working with design, research, and engineering to make complicated interactions easier to understand and use. You can reason through technical trade-offs with engineers and translate complex product and technical decisions into clear language for different audiences. You use research and data to test assumptions, measure impact, and make sound decisions when evidence is incomplete. You have led work across teams with different priorities and can build productive relationships with technical and business partners. You can turn an ambiguous problem into a clear strategy, make difficult prioritization decisions, follow through on delivery, and contribute to an inclusive and collaborative product community.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in London or Stockholm We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.

At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

Everything we do is driven by our love for music and podcasting. Today, we are the world’s most popular audio streaming subscription service.

Spotify's Content Business team helps bring compelling audio and video content to audiences around the world. Working across Spotify Originals, The Ringer, and licensed content, the team partners with creators, production companies, and internal stakeholders to bring content opportunities to life.
We're looking for a Manager, Content Acquisition to help turn content opportunities into completed deals. You'll manage the deal process from agreed commercial terms through contract execution, working closely with Legal, Finance, Studios, and external partners. This role combines commercial judgment, contract management, and financial analysis to support Spotify's growing content business.

What You'll Do:
Manage the execution of original and licensed content deals, from agreed commercial terms through final contracts, signatures, and close. Review, draft, and coordinate revisions to production, licensing, and talent agreements in partnership with Legal. Keep deals moving by tracking progress, identifying outstanding issues, and coordinating next steps with internal teams and external partners. Prepare clear deal documentation, including term sheets, deal summaries, approval materials, and stakeholder updates. Partner with Studios, Finance, Advertising, Partnerships, and Legal to resolve commercial questions and complete agreements. Support the evaluation of new content opportunities through financial models, business cases, and presentations. Monitor content budgets and financial commitments, identify differences against forecasts, and share insights to support informed decisions. Build productive relationships with talent representatives, production companies, and rights holders throughout the deal execution process.

Who You Are:
You have 2+ years of experience in entertainment, media, digital content, business affairs, content acquisition, or deal operations. You understand content licensing, production agreements, and the commercial considerations involved in developing and distributing audio or video content. You're comfortable reviewing term sheets and contracts, identifying key issues, and working with Legal to resolve them. You can manage multiple deals and deadlines while keeping stakeholders informed and maintaining accurate records. You have experience with financial analysis, budget tracking, or financial modeling and can turn data into practical recommendations. You communicate clearly and can explain complex commercial terms to colleagues with different areas of expertise. You enjoy working collaboratively with creative, commercial, legal, and finance teams to solve problems and move projects forward. You bring sound judgment, attention to detail, and a proactive approach to managing priorities in a changing environment.

Where You'll Be:
This role can be based in Los Angeles or NYC We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

lists.content:
• Manage the execution of original and licensed content deals, from agreed commercial terms through final contracts, signatures, and close.

  • Review, draft, and coordinate revisions to production, licensing, and talent agreements in partnership with Legal.

  • Keep deals moving by tracking progress, identifying outstanding issues, and coordinating next steps with internal teams and external partners.

  • Prepare clear deal documentation, including term sheets, deal summaries, approval materials, and stakeholder updates.

  • Partner with Studios, Finance, Advertising, Partnerships, and Legal to resolve commercial questions and complete agreements.

  • Support the evaluation of new content opportunities through financial models, business cases, and presentations.

  • Monitor content budgets and financial commitments, identify differences against forecasts, and share insights to support informed decisions.

  • Build productive relationships with talent representatives, production companies, and rights holders throughout the deal execution process.

• You have 2+ years of experience in entertainment, media, digital content, business affairs, content acquisition, or deal operations.

  • You understand content licensing, production agreements, and the commercial considerations involved in developing and distributing audio or video content.

  • You're comfortable reviewing term sheets and contracts, identifying key issues, and working with Legal to resolve them.

  • You can manage multiple deals and deadlines while keeping stakeholders informed and maintaining accurate records.

  • You have experience with financial analysis, budget tracking, or financial modeling and can turn data into practical recommendations.

  • You communicate clearly and can explain complex commercial terms to colleagues with different areas of expertise.

  • You enjoy working collaboratively with creative, commercial, legal, and finance teams to solve problems and move projects forward.

  • You bring sound judgment, attention to detail, and a proactive approach to managing priorities in a changing environment.

• This role can be based in Los Angeles or NYC
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. *Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Working closely with our VP of Finance Strategy & Operations, Chief Financial Officer (CFO), and executive team, you'll be a senior individual contributor with broad ownership of investor communications and relationships. You'll connect insights from across the business to explain our technical products, evolving business models, and long-term investment thesis. What You’ll Do Lead key workstreams of the quarterly earnings process, including messaging, scripts, questions and answers, data collection and synthesis, and conference call preparation; build repeatable processes with Finance, Legal, and executive leadership. Gather insights from research and development, Product, Sales, and other business leaders to explain GitLab's strategy, technical products, and business model transitions in investor communications and board materials. Own relationships with sell-side analysts and the investment community, monitor analyst models and consensus against our forecast, and flag gaps or risks to the head of IR and CFO. Prepare the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), CFO, and other executives for investor meetings, conferences, and roadshows; lead investor calls independently when executives aren't available, explaining how GitLab's business works and answering investor questions. Analyze peer and competitor earnings, Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings, and investor days; maintain benchmarking analyses and deliver quantitative and qualitative insights for executive and board discussions. Track GitLab's shareholder base and recommend investor targeting strategies to expand and maintain key ownership positions. Draft and review earnings decks, shareholder letters, fact sheets, and IR website content; partner with Finance, Legal, Communications, and Strategy to keep messaging consistent, accurate, and compliant with disclosure requirements, including Regulation Fair Disclosure (Regulation FD). Plan and deliver Investor Day with the head of IR to communicate GitLab's long-term story, alongside investor outreach, non-deal roadshows, and corporate access events. Financial modeling, valuation, and quantitative analysis skills, with the ability to identify the business drivers that shape investor expectations. Experience producing or analyzing earnings materials and investor presentations, and explaining technical software products, evolving business models, and financial performance clearly in writing and conversation. Proficiency with presentation and spreadsheet tools, experience with IR and market data platforms, and experience using artificial intelligence (AI) to improve workflows or a willingness to develop that capability. The ability to work independently and manage competing priorities in an all-remote, asynchronous-first environment, with an approach that reflects GitLab's values, especially transparency and efficiency. Nice to have: prior experience building an internal IR function. rows.description:
The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we're behind some of Spotify's most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you'll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them. Surfaces Moments is a ML team within the Personalization Mission focused on creating moment-based experiences across Spotify surfaces. The team owns and evolves the experiences that help listeners quickly connect with the content that matters most to them, including the Home Shortcuts experience and the underlying intelligence that powers it. By combining cutting-edge machine learning, recommendation systems, and product thinking, the team delivers highly relevant, personalized experiences to millions of listeners around the world. As a Staff Machine Learning Engineer, you will help shape the future of personalized discovery and engagement at Spotify. You'll work at the intersection of recommendation systems, large language models, and production-scale machine learning infrastructure to build experiences that delight users and drive meaningful impact. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys taking models from research to production, driving technical direction in ambiguous problem spaces, and solving complex personalization challenges at global scale.

What You'll Do:
Own and improve the machine learning models and systems that power the Home feed, including the Shortcuts experience. Design, build, and ship personalized recommendations that serve millions of Spotify listeners globally. Build content recommendation systems for emerging agentic and AI-powered user experiences. Train, fine-tune, evaluate, and optimize large language models using techniques such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT), distillation, and parameter-efficient training approaches. Partner closely with product managers, engineers, data scientists, and designers to define and execute experimentation strategies. Drive A/B testing, monitoring, model evaluation, and continuous optimization of recommendation quality, reliability, and cost efficiency. Improve ML platform capabilities, data pipelines, and production systems that support personalization at Spotify scale. Drive technical direction in ambiguous problem spaces and contribute to the long-term architecture of personalization systems. Mentor and support other machine learning engineers, helping raise the bar across the team.

Who You Are:
You have 8+ years of experience building and deploying machine learning systems in production environments. You have deep expertise in recommendation systems, ranking models, personalization, or large-scale content discovery platforms. You have strong proficiency in Python and hands-on experience building machine learning systems with PyTorch. You are experienced with large language model training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and optimization techniques including SFT, distillation, and LoRA. You have worked with large-scale inference systems and understand the challenges of latency, reliability, and cost optimization. You care deeply about creating high-quality user experiences through thoughtful application of machine learning. You communicate effectively across technical and non-technical audiences, and you influence technical decisions beyond your immediate team You know how to design, execute, and interpret online experiments and A/B tests to improve user outcomes. You have experience operating distributed machine learning workloads using technologies such as Ray, FSDP, HSDP, or similar frameworks. You are experienced building and maintaining data pipelines and orchestration workflows using technologies such as Flyte, Airflow, BigQuery, and cloud-based storage platforms.

Where You'll Be:
We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! For this role, you can be within the North Americas region as long as we have a work location. This team operates within the Eastern Standard time zone for collaboration.

rows.description:
How does a company with thousands of people building hundreds of products stay focused on what matters most? That's the question the Company Planning and Execution (CPE) team works on every day. We design the systems, processes, and insights that help Spotify plan, prioritise, and deliver at scale.
As a Data Scientist on CPE, you'll sit at the intersection of data, strategy, and operations. You'll bring clarity to complex questions by turning operational and strategic information into clear stories, recommendations, and decision frameworks that help leaders and teams act faster and smarter. You'll also explore how AI and automation can change the way people access insights and make decisions.
You'll work closely with data scientists, engineers, PMs, and business partners across the company to help refine how Spotify executes at scale. If you like making sense of ambiguity, care about how organisations work, and want your analysis to shape real decisions, this is the role.

What You'll Do:
Formulate hypotheses related to how Spotify plans and delivers, and communicate insights effectively to a range of audiences. Apply analytical techniques — including statistical models and machine learning — to identify trends and generate insights that improve how we work. Build and maintain the data models, pipelines, and dashboards that provide visibility into how Spotify plans and executes. Develop structured narratives and recommendations — not just charts, but the "why" and "so what" — in our semi-annual Planning and Execution Insight reports and recurring briefings. Explore how AI and automation can make insights faster to produce and easier to access across the company.

Who You Are:
Curious about how organisations work — not just the data, but the decisions and systems behind it. 5+ years of experience with a quantitative background in science, economics, engineering, or a related field. Strong interpersonal skills and comfortable working with multiple stakeholders across levels and functions. Able to take messy, complex datasets and turn them into clear recommendations and stories that land with non-technical audiences. Proficient in SQL and Python, comfortable in BigQuery, and experienced with tools like dbt, Tableau, or Looker. Experience with operational or work management data is a plus.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in London. We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best, with 2–3 days per week in the office.

rows.description:
Senior Fullstack Engineer – Internationalisation Platform
 
The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.
Within Platform, the Internationalisation team makes Spotify feel local everywhere. We build the systems, tools, and frameworks that power language support, localization workflows, cultural adaptation, and global feature rollouts across more than 180 markets. Our work ensures that when Spotify launches something new, it resonates just as well in São Paulo as it does in Stockholm.
We’re looking for a Senior Fullstack Engineer who cares deeply about building scalable systems and seamless user experiences — and who understands that great internationalisation is both a technical and cultural challenge.

What You'll Do:
Design, build, and evolve the platforms and services that power localization, translation workflows, and global content delivery across Spotify Develop high-quality frontend and backend solutions that enable product teams to ship globally from day one Partner closely with product managers, designers, and engineers across missions to ensure internationalisation is embedded early in the development lifecycle Improve developer experience by creating intuitive tooling, documentation, and self-serve frameworks Drive technical direction for complex cross-platform initiatives that impact millions of users worldwide Identify performance, scalability, and reliability improvements in systems supporting global expansion Contribute to a culture of technical excellence, knowledge sharing, and continuous learning

Who You Are:
You have 5+ years of experience building and shipping production-grade software as a fullstack engineer You are experienced with modern frontend frameworks (such as React) and backend development (such as Java, Kotlin, TypeScript, or similar technologies) You have a deep understanding of distributed systems, APIs, and scalable service architecture You know how to design systems with global scale, localization, and performance in mind You care about developer experience and building tools that empower other engineers You have worked in cross-functional environments and communicate complex ideas clearly You demonstrate strong technical judgment and take ownership of outcomes You care about building inclusive products that serve users across languages, regions, and cultures

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in London or Stockholm We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.
 
At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

Reporting to an Area Sales Manager or Regional Director, you’ll use a consultative approach to understand complex customer needs, guide them through evaluation, and coordinate pre- and post-sales resources to ensure successful deployments and visible business outcomes. The team is responsible for the full relationship lifecycle with enterprise accounts, from initial engagement through long-term expansion and advocacy, ensuring customers realize value from GitLab’s DevSecOps platform. Team members work in an all-remote, distributed environment and collaborate asynchronously across time zones with sales leadership, solutions architects, customer success, marketing, and channel partners. The team is currently focused on maintaining and growing our existing footprint in the region, executing a consistent global sales motion while adapting to local customer needs and partnering closely with strategic channel organizations to reach and support key accounts.How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being Flexible Paid Time Off Team Member Resource Groups Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan Growth and Development Fund Parental Leave Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application. Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process. Privacy Policy: Please review our Recruitment Privacy Policy. Your privacy is important to us. GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. rows.description:
At Spotify, we believe that music, podcasts, and culture move the world. We’re looking for a Content Marketing Manager to shape how Spotify shows up across Indonesia’s social platforms. You’ll help bring Spotify’s music, podcast, and cultural moments to life through storytelling that Indonesian audiences want to follow, engage with, and share.
 
Based in Jakarta and reporting to the Content & Social Marketing Lead - Indonesia, you’ll be a hands-on member of the team, turning cultural insights and marketing priorities into locally relevant content. You’ll work closely with agency partners, creators, artists, labels, and teams across Spotify to develop and deliver content across TikTok, Instagram, X, and emerging channels. You’ll combine strong creative instincts with performance insights to understand what’s working, adapt quickly, and keep Spotify relevant in fast-moving cultural conversations.

What You'll Do:
Own the day-to-day execution of Spotify Indonesia’s social channels across Meta, TikTok, X, and emerging platforms, helping strengthen Spotify’s position as a go-to platform for music and podcast fans in Indonesia. Contribute to Spotify’s social voice and presence in Indonesia, creating culturally relevant, platform-native storytelling that feels authentic to local audiences while remaining consistent with Spotify’s brand. Lead content marketing initiatives tied to artist and podcast releases, live events, editorial moments, and on-platform campaigns, including video content from ideation through distribution. Spot cultural trends, fandom signals, emerging formats, and conversations early, translating them into relevant content opportunities for Spotify. Brief and collaborate with agencies and internal cross-functional teams to develop and produce content across social and other relevant media channels. Build and maintain relationships with artists, labels, podcast and video creators, agencies, and internal partners, identifying opportunities for content and co-creation while managing expectations and keeping projects moving. Navigate a high-volume stakeholder environment across Marketing, Creative, Editorial, artist and label partnerships, and global teams while maintaining alignment and delivering at pace. Use data and performance insights to evaluate content, optimize approaches, and clearly communicate learnings and recommendations to internal partners. Share learnings and best practices with regional and global teams, contributing to how Spotify approaches content and social marketing across markets.

Who You Are:
You have 7+ years of experience in content marketing, including social media, with experience spanning strategy and creative work in Indonesia. You have a strong understanding of Indonesia’s digital and social landscape, fandom behavior, cultural conversations, and the ways audiences engage across different platforms. You have experience working with creators, agencies, and cross-functional teams to deliver impactful social and content campaigns. You’re confident planning and developing social media and content marketing strategies that can extend across other relevant media channels. You have strong creative instincts and are deeply connected to internet culture, music, podcasts, and fandoms, with an eye for emerging trends, formats, and conversations. You’re comfortable using data and insights to inform creative decisions, measure performance, and optimize campaigns. You’re skilled at managing multiple stakeholders across internal teams, external partners, agencies, and creator ecosystems. You’re organized and comfortable managing multiple projects and priorities in a fast-moving environment. You have strong communication skills in Bahasa Indonesia and English. You’re familiar with Spotify as a product and understand how audiences use and engage with the platform. Experience across broader marketing and media channels, including creator and influencer marketing, will help you thrive in this role.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in Jakarta. We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

rows.role: Senior Machine Learning Engineering Manager - Content Platform
rows.description:
We design Spotify's consumer experience—end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints—from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify.
You'll lead a senior-heavy group of 10–12 machine learning engineers, including Staff engineers, who team up dynamically to solve high-priority business problems while staying deep in content understanding (audio, video and text). This is a player-coach role with a strong strategic remit: you'll shape where the group goes next, grow our audio understanding expertise over the long term, and help the team scale through thoughtful, practical use of AI in everyday engineering work.

What You'll Do:
Lead, coach and grow a group of 10+ senior and Staff machine learning engineers who team up dynamically around business problems while staying deep in their domain. Set technical and team strategy for multiple content understanding problems and turn it into clear, achievable plans. Own delivery of high-priority company initiatives, from shaping the problem through to measurable impact for listeners. Stay close to the technology as a player-coach. Lead technical strategy, reviewing designs, guiding modelling and retrieval choices, and contributing hands-on where it helps the team most. Define and champion a practical point of view on how ML engineers use AI tools in their day-to-day work, and help the team realise real productivity gains. Partner with product, design, research and other engineering leaders across Spotify to align priorities and share context.

Who You Are:
You have deep machine learning expertise and Staff-level technical judgement, and you're comfortable getting hands-on when it matters. You bring experience across NLP, audio / music content understanding and recommender systems. You have a track record of managing engineering teams while delivering complex, cross-functional initiatives. You enjoy coaching senior and Staff engineers, and you help experienced people grow their impact. You have a clear, informed point of view on using AI to improve how ML engineers work, and you can inspire a team to adopt it. You think strategically, communicate clearly, and can balance long-term bets with near-term delivery.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in London or Stockholm. We offer the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meeetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

rows.description:
Spotify's in-house creative studio, Reverb, brings our brand to life through thoughtful design, visual storytelling, and creative production. Working across brand and communications, the team creates work that connects with audiences around the world.
We're looking for a Global Creative Lead to shape the visual direction of Reverb and lead a talented team of graphic designers, motion designers, and producers. You'll combine creative vision with hands-on leadership, helping the team deliver distinctive, high-quality work while building an environment where people can collaborate, experiment, and grow.
Reporting to the Director, Global Experiential & Content Production, you'll play a key role in shaping the studio's creative output and how we work together.

What You'll Do:
Lead and develop a team of approximately 5–6 graphic designers, motion designers, and producers, supporting their creative growth and career development. Shape the visual and motion design direction across Reverb projects, creating distinctive work that brings Spotify's brand and stories to life. Partner with teams across brand, communications, marketing, and production to turn creative briefs into engaging visual experiences across channels and formats. Guide creative development from concept through delivery, providing clear direction, constructive feedback, and thoughtful design decisions. Manage project intake, priorities, budgets, timelines, and resources to help the team deliver meaningful work across multiple projects. Collaborate with Reverb's creative and production leads to build a connected, effective studio and a consistent creative experience. Present creative concepts and recommendations to senior stakeholders, explaining the thinking behind decisions and building alignment. Work with internal teams and external creative partners to maintain design quality, manage production needs, and navigate relevant legal and licensing requirements.

Who You Are:
You bring 8+ years of experience in graphic design, visual design, or a related creative discipline, with a portfolio demonstrating strong visual storytelling, brand identity, and motion design. You have 4+ years of experience leading creative teams, with a thoughtful approach to coaching, feedback, and helping others develop their craft. You're comfortable shaping creative direction across digital, social, advertising, editorial, and long-form brand content, adapting your approach to different audiences and formats. You have experience using Adobe Creative Cloud, Figma, and relevant visual or motion design tools, and you're curious about how emerging technologies can support the creative process. You know how to balance creative ambition with practical delivery, making thoughtful decisions around timelines, budgets, and resources. You communicate creative ideas clearly and enjoy collaborating with designers, producers, and partners across different disciplines and regions. You have experience working with external creative studios, production companies, and partners, including managing budgets, contracts, and production workflows. You care about creating an inclusive, supportive team environment where different perspectives are valued, feedback is welcomed, and people can do their best work.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in New York City. We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! We ask that you come into the office 1-2x per week.

The United States base range for this position is $123,189.00–$175,985.00 USD, plus equity. The benefits available for this position include health insurance, six-month paid parental leave, 401(k) retirement plan, monthly meal allowance, 23 paid days off, paid flexible holidays, and paid sick leave. These ranges may be modified in the future.


Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.
 
At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

rows.role: Senior Product Manager - Audiobooks Format Foundations
rows.description:
We design Spotify’s consumer experience - end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints—from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify. We’re seeking a Senior Product Manager to help lead the audiobook experience across Spotify’s mobile apps. You’ll join Format Foundations within Core Experience and partner closely with the Audiobooks business unit to shape how listeners discover, evaluate, enjoy, and build lasting relationships with audiobooks on Spotify.

What You'll Do:
Lead product strategy for Spotify’s audiobook experience, shaping how the format becomes more engaging, valuable, and enjoyable for listeners, creators, and the business. Define and evolve the experience across the audiobook journey, from discovery and evaluation through playback, library management, and reading. Partner closely with the Audiobooks business unit to translate business strategy and listener needs into product innovation that supports growth. Drive innovation across multimodal experiences, including the intersection of listening and reading. Partner with Engineering, Design, Data, and other cross-functional teams to deliver intuitive, high-quality experiences at scale. Use data, experimentation, and user insights to make informed product decisions and continuously improve the experience. Build alignment across Core Experience, Audiobooks, Personalization, and other partners to create a cohesive Spotify experience. Lead complex cross-functional initiatives end to end, setting direction and scope, creating alignment, and partnering with Engineering on delivery.

Who You Are:
You have 5+ years of product management experience, including meaningful experience with audiobook, ebook, digital reading, or related consumer products. You have a deep understanding of the audiobook or digital reading landscape, including user behavior, publisher ecosystems, and competitive dynamics. You have experience building consumer products for mobile platforms such as iOS and Android, including complex user experiences. You understand how to build scalable systems and experiences that help teams move faster. You know how to balance user needs, technical considerations, and business impact when making product decisions. You care deeply about creating intuitive, high-quality consumer experiences at scale. You have partnered closely with Engineering, Design, Data, and other disciplines to bring products from strategy through delivery. You are comfortable navigating ambiguity, making thoughtful trade-offs, and creating clarity across teams. You can influence stakeholders across functions and levels to build alignment and drive meaningful outcomes. You actively use AI tools in your product development workflow, including for research, analysis, iteration, and prototyping.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in Stockholm or London We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

rows.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.About the role As an Applied AI Solutions Architect supporting a dedicated national security mission program, you will be the customer's trusted technical advisor — helping them understand the value of Claude and how to successfully integrate and deploy it into their technology stack. You'll combine deep technical and cyber domain expertise with customer-facing skills to architect LLM solutions for complex mission challenges while maintaining our high standards for safety and reliability. Working closely with our Sales, Product, and Engineering teams, you'll guide the customer from technical discovery through successful deployment, much of it on-site in secure environments. rows.description:
The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.
 
Security engineers at Spotify protect our platform, employees, creators, and more than 700 million users. We are looking for an experienced Security Engineer to join the Detection and Response organization and help identify, investigate, and respond to threats across Spotify's environment.
 
You will work within our detection engineering squad where the team owns alert triage, security investigations, threat hunting, and the detection engineering lifecycle. You will turn threat intelligence, incident learnings, and analyst feedback into effective detections and investigation workflows. You will partner closely with the detection infrastructure squad, which builds and operates Detection and Response platforms and telemetry pipelines, and with teams across Spotify to make sure your squad has the signals and capabilities needed to detect and respond to threats at Spotify's scale.
 
We are a distributed team that values curiosity, sound judgment, clear communication, and continuous learning. We teach and learn from one another, adapt as the threat landscape changes, and focus our effort according to business needs and risk.

What You'll Do:
Identify detection opportunities, define clear telemetry requirements, and partner with the detection infrastructure squad and data owners to make the signals needed for detection and investigation available. Develop, test, tune, and maintain detections across endpoint, identity, cloud, SaaS, email, and other security-relevant environments. Investigate and prioritize alerts, determine their security impact, and participate in incident containment and remediation. Build repeatable investigation workflows and playbooks for alert triage, evidence collection, decision-making, escalation, containment, and response. Improve proactive threat-identification and threat-hunting capabilities using internal telemetry and external threat intelligence. Create cutting-edge AI workflows for Detection and Response that enrich alerts, gather and analyze evidence, guide investigations, and automate repetitive response work while preserving appropriate human judgment and oversight. Measure detection effectiveness, identify coverage gaps, and tune detections to balance security value, fidelity, and analyst workload. Use SIEM, EDR, SOAR, and related security platforms to research threats, develop detections, investigate alerts, and validate security outcomes. Share knowledge, document decisions, and communicate security findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

Who You Are:
You are curious, collaborative, and comfortable making progress in an ambiguous and rapidly changing environment. You have 3+ years of hands-on experience in security operations, incident response, threat detection, detection engineering, or closely related work. You understand how analysts triage and investigate alerts and how detection quality affects their decisions and workload. You know how to create and tune detections based on attacker behavior, available telemetry, and an expected investigation path. You are experienced with security platforms such as SIEM, EDR, SOAR, or comparable monitoring and response technologies. You can write code or use an automation platform to analyze security telemetry, enrich alerts, build investigation workflows, and remove repetitive work. Experience with Python or a similar language is valuable. You understand modern detection-as-code practices, including GitHub, peer review, CI/CD, testing, and safely managing production detection content. You have experience working with at least one major cloud platform, such as Google Cloud, AWS, or Azure. You understand common threats affecting SaaS-oriented corporate and production environments. You care about clear documentation, inclusive collaboration, and explaining security concepts to people with different backgrounds and levels of expertise. You are excited to create and critically evaluate cutting-edge AI workflows for detection development, alert triage, security investigations, and response, while applying sound security judgment and appropriate human oversight.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in New York We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

The United States base range for this position is $132,948–$189,927 USD, plus equity. The benefits available for this position include health insurance, six-month paid parental leave, 401(k) retirement plan, monthly meal allowance, 23 paid days off, paid flexible holidays, and paid sick leave. These ranges may be modified in the future.


Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.
 
At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

At Spotify, our Subscriptions organisation helps listeners discover the value of Spotify, find the right subscription, and keep enjoying the content they love. From acquisition and activation to retention, commerce, and customer service, we build experiences that connect listeners with Spotify and support lasting relationships.
We're looking for an Engineering Manager II to lead a team of data and backend engineers within our Subscriptions Mission. Your team will build data products, pipelines, and services that help teams understand listener needs and deliver more relevant experiences. You'll work closely with product managers, data scientists, business partners, and engineers to turn complex challenges into reliable solutions. You'll also create an environment where engineers can grow, collaborate, and make a meaningful impact.

What You'll Do:
Lead, support, and develop a team of data and backend engineers, creating an inclusive environment where everyone can contribute and grow. Work with product managers, business partners, and engineering teams to set priorities and build data products that improve the subscription experience. Guide the development of reliable, scalable data pipelines and backend services that support targeting, messaging, personalisation, and machine learning. Help your team make informed technical decisions, balancing data quality, reliability, business needs, and long-term maintainability. Support engineers through regular feedback, coaching, career development, and opportunities to share knowledge. Collaborate across teams to manage dependencies, solve challenges, and build shared data solutions. Improve engineering practices, including service reliability, sustainable on-call processes, and responsible data management. Explore opportunities to use AI and automation to simplify workflows, improve data quality, and support your team's work.

Who You Are:
You have experience leading data or backend engineering teams and enjoy helping engineers develop their skills and careers. You have a background in software or data engineering and can guide technical discussions about data architecture, distributed systems, scalability, and reliability. You understand how to balance team development, technical decisions, and delivery priorities to achieve meaningful results. You have worked with large-scale data pipelines, data platforms, or backend services. Experience with technologies such as Google Cloud, BigQuery, Apache Beam, Dataflow, dbt, Flyte, Airflow, Scala, or Java is valuable. You can navigate changing priorities, make informed decisions, and help your team move forward when the path isn't always clear. You communicate clearly and build effective partnerships with product, business, and engineering teams to turn shared goals into practical solutions. You value different perspectives, encourage open feedback, and help create an environment where people feel respected and supported. You're curious about new technologies, including AI and automation, and enjoy finding ways to improve how teams work and deliver value.

Where You'll Be:
We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! For this role, you can be within the EMEA region as long as we have a work location (excluding France due to on-call restrictions). This team operates within the Central European and GMT time zone for collaboration.

The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.
The Data Platform team develops and maintains the infrastructure that supports Spotify’s data ecosystem. Within Data Platform, the Data Collection product area builds infrastructure that makes it easier to collect and consume data at scale. You’ll join a team focused on making user behaviour data seamless and reliable for data teams across Spotify.

What You'll Do:
Collaborate with product and engineering teams to build and support critical data infrastructure and datasets. Build systems that collect and process user behaviour data at scale. Help power Spotify’s personalization and recommendation systems, as well as the tools teams use to build and test new features. Design and evolve data architectures that support high data volumes and a broad range of internal users. Improve the reliability, scalability, and usability of our data infrastructure. Work across disciplines to solve complex data challenges and make an impact across Spotify.

Who You Are:
You are an experienced Data Engineer, and proficient in backend development using Java. You are comfortable working with large-scale datasets using SQL and platforms such as BigQuery. You have experience with JVM-based data processing frameworks such as Flink, Beam, Dataflow, or Spark. You are familiar with DevOps practices, cloud infrastructure, containerized applications, and Kubernetes fundamentals. You have experience with data modeling and schema design. You care about high-quality code and engineering practices such as continuous delivery and automated testing. You value experimentation, iterative development, and collaborative software development practices. You are comfortable navigating ambiguity and open-ended problems, using data and sound judgment to make decisions.

This role is based in London We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

rows.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.About the role Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us. DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it. You'll be the engineer who owns autonomous systems across that footprint as one security domain, from both sides: drones, ground robots and automated vehicles for patrol, inspection and moving hardware, including the security of that automation inside secure areas, and the detection systems that tell us what is flying over or operating near a site uninvited. You set the approach, select and integrate the platforms and sensors, write the requirements vendors build to, and run what you ship, from the operating model where operators assign missions and machines carry them out to the playbook that turns a detection into an identified track and a well-evidenced handoff to whoever holds authority over the airspace. Interdiction is not part of this role. The goal is security that runs itself: coverage, fleet health and evidence verified continuously, with tools and AI agents doing the routine triage. We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones. We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well. You'll work with the rest of DCSE, including its physical security systems engineers and the engineers on its security monitoring platform, with Anthropic's data center operations and legal teams, and directly with site operators, equipment vendors and aviation and public safety authorities. The role is based in San Francisco, with remote applicants in the US considered, and involves regular travel to data center sites, which are critical infrastructure. Key responsibilities Autonomous security and inspection systems: own the drones, ground robots and other autonomous platforms for perimeter patrol, incident response and infrastructure inspection: platform selection, operating model, operator qualification, maintenance, and the data path from machine to analyst Tools, automation and AI agents: build the integrations that carry detections, tracks, telemetry and fleet health into the team's security monitoring platform, and the tools and agents that triage detections, check fleet health and assemble evidence. When a review keeps costing people time, you build the tool or agent that retires it Detection of uncrewed systems: engineer the sensing that tells us what is flying over or operating near a site, what it is and who needs to know: sensor selection and evaluation against live targets, per-site coverage, classification and false-alarm handling, and the playbook from first detection to handoff,
