Principal Engineers at GitLab are recognized experts across multiple technology domains and represent the senior technical leadership within their organization. In this role you will set technical direction for a significant part of the Agent Platform, working across several teams to turn agentic capabilities into something engineering organizations can actually depend on: predictable, observable, governable, and fast enough to sit in the critical path of real development work. The Agent Platform is not a single service. It spans agent execution and orchestration, flow definition and event-driven triggering, the AI Catalog through which customers discover and manage agents, model routing and evaluation, and the governance surface that decides which agents may act where and under whose identity. It runs on GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, and Self-Managed installations, including deployments that use self-hosted models to meet compliance requirements. You will work on the parts of that system where the hard architectural questions live, and you will do it hands-on. This role reports into the VP of the AI Engineering organization and works closely with Engineering Managers, Staff Engineers, Product Management, Infrastructure and Security. What you'll do Define the technical direction for a significant area of Duo Agent Platform across several teams, and partner with Engineering Managers and Product to turn it into a roadmap with a six-month horizon. Build the orchestration layer that makes agents and flows reliable: session lifecycle, tool invocation, context assembly, concurrency, retries, timeouts, and failure modes that degrade gracefully instead of stalling a developer's workflow. Hands on work on driving topics throughout the whole organisation from POC level, architecture to full implementation. Participate in Incident Management on-call rotation, to help meet availability goals for GitLab.com. Strong product builder and ownership mentality. Understanding of product strategy, technical strategy, delivering customer value and iteration towards a successful product Write clear, opinionated design documents, architecture narratives, and decision records that let other teams make aligned decisions. Ensure the architecture holds across multi-tenant GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed deployments, including self-hosted model configurations, and respects data governance boundaries in each. Use the platform on our own work, find where it falls short of what we claim, and feed that back through improvements into the product. Mentor Staff and Senior Engineers, and raise the bar for experimentation rigor and cross-team collaboration. Work across the whole platform on different projects, features and teams. This reaches across: Design the extensibility surface so customers can build custom agents and flows, connect their own tools and internal systems, and bring external agents such as Claude Code and Codex into GitLab workflows without weakening the platform's guarantees. Drive down the cost and latency of agentic requests, and work with Product on how model selection, routing, and credit consumption behave as usage grows. Define the evaluation practice for the platform: offline benchmarks and online experiments that measure task completion, correctness, tool-call accuracy, latency, and cost per task, and that catch regressions before customers do. Build the governance and safety surface with Security and Compliance: policy-driven controls over which agents and models may run where, permission and identity semantics that align to existing roles and group structure, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, traceability of every flow session, and audit that stands up to enterprise review. Complete Interview Training and participate in hiring for the department as a technical interviewer or panel member. What you'll bring 8+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years at Staff, Principal level or equivalent senior technical leadership. Hands-on production experience building on large language models: agent loops, tool calling, context management, retrieval, prompt and model evaluation. Experience shipping this to real users, not only prototyping it. Strong background in distributed systems, including service decomposition, fault tolerance, observability, and operational resilience under multi-tenant load. A track record of defining evaluation frameworks and using benchmark and experiment results to make architecture decisions, rather than shipping on intuition. Experience designing human-in-the-loop controls, safety guardrails, and responsible AI practices for systems that act on a customer's behalf. Ability to drive alignment across Engineering, Product, Infrastructure, and Security on problems that start out ambiguous. Experience mentoring senior engineers and shaping technical direction across multiple teams without direct authority. Comfort working in one or more of Ruby, Go, Python, or TypeScript, and willingness to work across the stack the platform spans. Excellent written and asynchronous communication, and the ability to work effectively in a fully remote, globally distributed organization. About the team The AI engineering organisation is building the product and infrastructure that make GitLab an effective environment for running agents across the software development lifecycle. We’re distributed across the world and partner with teams throughout GitLab to help the GitLab Duo Agent Platform become the backbone of GitLab's AI features. It is a relationship role: your job is to make Anthropic a trusted, visible, and valued neighbor, from the earliest stages of site selection through construction and long-term operations. You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly. Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand. You will travel regularly within Virginia and West Virginia, up to 50% of the time, and occasionally to other Anthropic data center markets. municipal officials, state economic development agencies, community groups, civic leaders, educational institutions, and workforce partners in the Virginia and West Virginia data center markets you cover Develop and execute a community engagement strategy for each of your markets, spanning site selection, pre-development, construction, and ongoing operations Build external coalitions, host that scale as Anthropic's infrastructure footprint grows Minimum qualifications Experience in community affairs, public affairs, economic development, government relations, local or state government, Spotify Technology is our business-to-business software team, helping organizations improve how they build and deliver software. Our products, including Backstage Portal, Confidence, and Xirp, support developers and AI-powered systems as they navigate increasingly complex engineering environments.
As Sales Manager for our Enterprise team, you will lead the Account Executives who drive new business for Spotify Technology. Reporting to the Director of Sales, you'll set the strategy for how we win with organizations of 1,000+ employees, where buying committees span engineering, finance, procurement, security, and legal, and fewer, larger deals can take many months to close.
This is both a strategic and hands-on role: you'll shape our enterprise sales approach while staying close to the deals, coaching your team through complex opportunities and helping them close. You'll collaborate with Sales Engineering, Marketing, Product, Customer Success, and Revenue Operations to create a seamless customer experience. Your ability to develop sellers, run a disciplined sales process, and engage confidently with senior engineering leaders will be key to your success.

What You'll Do:
• Lead, coach, and develop a team of Enterprise Account Executives, helping each seller grow their skills and consistently achieve or exceed their targets. • Own quarterly and annual team revenue targets for new business with organizations of 1,000+ employees, in partnership with the Director of Sales. • Translate Spotify Technology's overall sales strategy into a clear enterprise plan, including target accounts, territory priorities, and account planning standards. • Build a team that converts inbound demand while proactively hunting new opportunities in target accounts. • Stay hands-on in key deals, joining customer meetings, supporting negotiations, and helping navigate complex buying committees. • Coach the team on strategic account planning, multi-threading, champion building, and developing executive-level business cases. • Run a disciplined operating rhythm through regular pipeline reviews, deal reviews, and one-on-ones, while maintaining accurate forecasts and a healthy, predictable pipeline for long-cycle deals. • Partner with Revenue Operations on territory design, reporting, and process improvements for the Enterprise segment. • Collaborate with Sales Engineering on technical evaluations and proofs of concept, with Customer Success on retention and expansion, and with Marketing on account-based programs and pipeline generation. • Help sellers articulate how Backstage Portal, Confidence, and Xirp solve developer experience challenges, including how AI is reshaping software development in large organizations. • Help sellers tell a compelling story about Spotify's internal approach to solving engineering challenges and how our products are proven internally at scale. • Share customer feedback with Product and internal teams to help shape the roadmap. • Contribute to hiring, onboarding, and developing sales playbooks as the Enterprise team grows.

Who You Are:
• You have 8+ years of experience in B2B SaaS sales, including closing large, complex enterprise deals, and 3+ years of experience managing sales teams. • You have a proven track record of building and developing high-performing teams that consistently achieve or exceed targets in enterprise environments. • You are both strategic and hands-on, comfortable setting direction while staying involved in the details of individual deals. • You bring strong judgment when working with incomplete information and can coach your team to prioritize high-potential opportunities while confidently moving away from poorly qualified deals. • You have experience selling to engineering leaders, CTOs, platform teams, or developer experience buyers, and understand how they evaluate and make purchasing decisions. • You are familiar with software development, Product Management, DevOps tools, or developer ecosystems. • You understand long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles, including procurement processes, security reviews, and multi-year agreements. • You have experience partnering closely with Sales Engineering and understand the importance of technical depth in complex enterprise sales. • You use data and metrics to guide forecasting, coaching, and decision-making, while building structure and processes without adding unnecessary complexity. • You bring strong communication, coaching, negotiation, and presentation skills. • You are excited to help build a scalable enterprise sales motion with AI and enjoy working with innovative products in an evolving technology landscape.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in New York City We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

The United States base range for this position is $143,510 - $205,015 plus equity. The benefits available for this position include health insurance, six month paid parental leave, 401(k) retirement plan, monthly meal allowance, 23 paid days off, 13 paid flexible holidays. These ranges may be modified in the future.

rows.description:
Spotify Technology is our business-to-business software team, helping organizations improve how they build and deliver software. Our products, including Backstage Portal, Confidence, and Xirp, support developers and AI-powered systems as they navigate increasingly complex engineering environments.
As an Account Executive on our Commercial team, you will drive new business for Spotify Technology. You'll focus on companies with fewer than 1,000 employees, where sales cycles typically run from weeks to a few months and success depends on a repeatable, scalable sales motion. You'll manage a high volume of opportunities, work with one or a small group of decision-makers (often a hands-on engineering leader or CTO), and move deals efficiently from the first conversation to close. You'll also help shape the playbook that enables our commercial business to grow.
You'll collaborate with Sales Engineering, Marketing, Product, and Customer Success to create a seamless customer experience. Your ability to quickly understand customers' technical needs and connect them to clear business value will be key to your success.

What You'll Do:
• Identify and pursue new business opportunities with companies of fewer than 1,000 employees. While significant inbound demand supports the pipeline, top performers will exceed targets by treating this as a “Hunter” role in addition to converting inbound demand. • Own the full sales cycle, from prospecting and discovery through demos, proposals, negotiations, and close. • Manage a high-velocity pipeline across multiple opportunities, keeping deals moving with clear next steps and maintaining accurate pipeline and forecast data in the CRM. • Achieve and exceed quarterly and annual revenue targets. • Run efficient, repeatable sales processes and contribute to playbooks that help scale our commercial sales motion. • Partner with Marketing on inbound and outbound pipeline generation, responding quickly to leads and identifying new opportunities. • Articulate how Backstage Portal and Confidence solve developer experience challenges, including how AI is reshaping software development. • Tell a compelling story about Spotify's internal approach to solving engineering challenges and how our products are proven internally at scale. • Present case studies and customer success stories that demonstrate the impact and business value of our products. • Partner with Sales Engineering on technical evaluations and ensure a smooth handoff to Customer Success to support onboarding, retention, and expansion. • Share customer feedback with Product and internal teams to help shape the roadmap.

Who You Are:
• You have 4+ years of experience in a quota-carrying sales role, including 2+ years in a revenue-closing role, ideally in SaaS, developer platforms, or cloud services. • You have a proven track record of achieving and exceeding targets in a fast-paced, high-volume B2B environment, ideally selling to small and medium-sized businesses (SMB) or mid-market companies. • You are skilled at managing fast sales cycles efficiently while maintaining a thoughtful and effective discovery process. • You bring strong judgment when working with incomplete information, allowing you to prioritize high-potential opportunities and confidently move away from poorly qualified deals. • You have experience selling to technical stakeholders, including CTOs, engineering leaders, developers, or DevOps teams. • You are familiar with software development, Product Management, DevOps tools, or developer ecosystems. • You can clearly communicate technical benefits and business value to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. • You bring strong communication, presentation, negotiation, and closing skills. • You are highly organized and disciplined in pipeline management, forecasting, and CRM hygiene. • You are excited to help build a scalable sales motion with AI and enjoy working with innovative products in an evolving technology landscape.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in London. We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

rows.role: Senior Staff Engineer - Platform & Partner Experience
rows.description:
We design Spotify's consumer experience — end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints — from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify.
Platform & Partner Experience (PPX) sits within the Experience Mission, shaping how Spotify shows up across devices, platforms, and partner ecosystems. We build the foundations that power seamless integrations — from smart speakers to cars to AI agents — while ensuring every interaction feels personal, reliable, and unmistakably Spotify. 
As a Senior Staff Engineer, you'll advance how our systems power partner experiences at scale, tackling complex challenges that span teams, systems and organizational boundaries. You will work closely with platform, infrastructure, and product teams across the company to create shared foundations, streamline our architecture and unlock new experiences for our users and partners.

What You Will Do:
Lead the technical strategy, architecture, and development of systems that enable and enhance partner and platform experiences across devices and integrations Drive complex technical initiatives that span multiple studios or a full mission — particularly where coordination cost, architectural sprawl, or competing local optimizations are part of the problem Create leverage by unifying fragmented approaches, retiring duplicative systems, and establishing the standards and platforms that enable multiple studios move faster without reinventing foundations — judging where consolidation creates leverage and where local autonomy is the better choice Define and influence technical strategy across organizational boundaries and bring other senior engineers along in executing it Collaborate with engineering, product and design leaders across the Experience Mission and beyond to identify shared opportunities, align technical direction and reduce duplication Shape how AI transforms the software development lifecycle and pioneer AI-native workflows and capabilities that bridge engineering, product, and design

Who You Are:
You have deep experience designing, building and operating distributed systems that serve users at scale You have a strong track record of technical leadership — influencing and shaping architecture decisions across teams, and driving organizational change in how software gets built You thrive in complex, ambiguous problem spaces and can identify where technical investment will create the greatest leverage across teams and systems You care deeply about reliable, high-quality user experiences powered by data and personalization You actively explore how AI reshapes how we build, not just what we build, and can turn emerging capabilities into practical improvements in how teams work You bring a thoughtful, collaborative, inclusive mindset and actively contribute to a positive team culture

Where You Will Be:
We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best. For this role, you can be based anywhere in EMEA where Spotify has a work location (excluding France due to on-call restrictions). The team collaborates within Central European and GMT time zones.

rows.description:
At Spotify, our Subscriptions Mission focuses on creating experiences that help listeners discover the value of Spotify, become subscribers, and stay with us for the long term. By combining technology, experimentation, and a deep understanding of our users, we help connect artists and fans while building a sustainable subscription business. Within the Subscriptions Mission, the Subs Foundational Models Product Area is part of the Subs User Understanding Studio. We build scalable machine learning solutions that personalize the subscriber journey, from conversion through to long-term retention. Working closely with teams across the mission, we develop ML solutions that improve key business metrics, including subscriber growth, monthly active users, and Premium retention. We're looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to join our Radius squad. You'll take ownership of impactful ML initiatives, develop and improve production models, and contribute to the foundational ML capabilities that power personalization and optimization across Subscriptions. Your work could include reducing friction for Free users while balancing retention and conversion, improving payment experiences to reduce Premium churn, or developing reusable models such as subscriber embeddings that support multiple products and use cases.

What You'll Do:
Lead multi-week ML initiatives end to end, from translating business requirements into technical specifications to shipping models and measuring their impact on subscriber metrics Own components of our ML systems, making independent technical trade-offs and keeping them observable, reliable, and well documented Collaborate with a multi-functional agile team spanning user research, design, data science, product management, and engineering to build new product features that advance our mission to connect artists and fans in personalised and relevant ways Prototype new approaches and productionise solutions at scale for our hundreds of millions of active users Help drive optimisation, testing, and tooling to improve quality Unblock and share context with your teammates to raise the whole squad's velocity Use AI-assisted engineering to move faster and remove repetitive toil, while owning the quality of everything you ship Partner closely with senior and staff ML engineers, and be part of an active group of machine learning practitioners in your mission and across Spotify

Who You Are:
You have experience building and shipping production ML systems You have a strong background in machine learning, theory, and practice You are comfortable explaining the intuition and assumptions behind ML concepts You can own well-scoped ML projects end to end and make sound technical decisions independently You communicate clearly with stakeholders and can explain the reasoning behind your technical choices You are curious, open to feedback, and keen to grow your scope over time You have hands-on experience implementing and maintaining production ML systems in Python, Scala, or similar languages, including model development with PyTorch You are experienced with building data pipelines, and you are self-sufficient in getting the data you need to build and evaluate your models You preferably have experience with cloud platforms like GCP or AWS You care about agile software processes, data development, reliability, and focused experimentation You have a desire to drive business impact

Where You'll Be:
We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! For this role, you can be within the EMEA region as long as we have a work location This team operates within the Central European and GMT time zone for collaboration.

Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.
 
At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

rows.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.About the role Anthropic's go-to-market engine runs on Salesforce: how leads become pipeline, how deals are tracked and forecast, how customers renew and expand, and how partners work alongside our sellers. As a Business Systems Analyst, you'll be responsible for how one of those core motions is represented in system, and a trusted partner to GTM leadership when they want to change how it works. We're looking for someone who operates at the intersection of three things: a strategist who can sit with GTM leaders and shape how they want to understand their part of the business, an analyst who can turn that into rigorous process and data design, and a builder who's comfortable enough in Salesforce to ship meaningful parts of it themselves. You can move fluidly between whiteboard, requirements doc, and admin console. You'll partner deeply with RevOps on the operating model and with our Salesforce developers on anything that needs code. Where you might sit We're hiring across several parts of the customer lifecycle. Placement depends on your background and where you can have the most impact. Opportunity Acceleration: Owns how deals are tracked, forecast, and credited in Salesforce, from stage design and forecasting to the ownership and team structures behind them. You'll partner with sales leadership to make pipeline something everyone can trust and sellers can work quickly. Lead-to-Pipeline: Owns how leads, inbound demand, and BDR outreach become qualified pipeline: lifecycle stages, routing and ownership, handoff rules, and the tools BDRs and sellers work in every day. You'll partner with BDR, marketing, and sales leadership to make the path from first touch to open opportunity faster and easier to measure. Post-Sales: Owns the systems behind renewals, expansion, and customer coverage: how post-sale opportunities are created, forecast, and worked by account management and customer success. You'll give post-sales leaders a clear, trustworthy view of the customer base and the tools to act on it. Partnerships: Owns how partner-sourced and co-sell deals are registered, attributed, and worked alongside our sellers, including the partner-facing processes and reporting leadership relies on. You'll help turn a fast-growing channel into a motion the business can measure and scale. Key responsibilities Own the design of your core funnel domain in Salesforce: lifecycle stages, process, exit and handoff criteria, key fields, and the automation and guardrails that keep the data trustworthy Partner with GTM leadership on how their motion runs and how they want to see it, and make the tradeoff calls on what teams enter versus what insight that data unlocks Partner with RevOps to systematize how GTM teams are structured, assigned, and credited: ownership, routing, coverage, splits, and the territory and role structures those depend on Operationalize the methodology in system, turning frameworks and process discipline into fields, validation, scoring, and in-context guidance that people actually use Act as data-model steward for your domain and its closest neighbors: the named approver for new fields, automation, and integrations touching those objects, and the keeper of why each one exists Build and ship declarative solutions yourself where that's the right call, and write specs clean enough that our developers can build the rest without five rounds of clarification Own the seams to the neighboring stages of the customer lifecycle (lead handoff, opportunity, quote-to-cash, renewal, partner attribution) so the experience is coherent end to end even where the build sits with another team Evaluate and configure tooling that accelerates the motion: routing, activity capture, sequencing, deal inspection, account planning Run discovery, UAT, enablement, and adoption measurement for everything you ship; help raise the bar for how BSA work is done on this team Minimum qualifications Experience in GTM/Revenue systems as a Business Systems Analyst, Sales Systems Lead, or RevOps Systems role, with real ownership of work in a core funnel domain such as lead management, opportunity and pipeline, renewals and account management, or partner channel Experience designing and rolling out a lifecycle, process model, or forecasting motion at a fast-growing company, owning it from discovery through enablement and adoption Credibility with GTM stakeholders: you've been in the pipeline review, forecast call, or planning session, and you can push back when there's a better answer Hands-on Salesforce skills, with comfort building meaningful parts of your own solution (Flow, validation, assignment and routing, page and Path design) and specs that make the handoff to developers clean Crisp communication across GTM teams, leadership, RevOps, and engineers, adjusting altitude for each Preferred qualifications 5+ years of experience in GTM/Revenue systems roles Salesforce Administrator certification Advanced Administrator, Business Analyst, or Sales Cloud Consultant certification Experience partnering with RevOps or Sales Strategy on team-structure questions (ownership, routing, splits, territory) and turning those decisions into working system design Experience across more than one part of the customer lifecycle, such as lead, opportunity, renewal, or partner Curiosity about AI-assisted systems work and eagerness to fold it into how you design, build, and document; prior hands-on use is a strong plus The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.Annual Salary:$270,000—$315,000 USDLogistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

rows.description:
What You’ll Do:
Own the AV experience across EMEA, including meeting rooms, boardrooms, common areas, labs, lounges, and digital signage. Provide thoughtful, high-quality AV support for executive and VIP meetings, helping ensure technology works reliably when it matters most. Design, document, deliver, and maintain AV solutions and technical standards in partnership with the global AV team. Review technical designs and documentation from external integrators to ensure solutions meet requirements. Lead AV initiatives and projects with internal partners and external vendors, from defining scope through delivery, commissioning, and handover. Act as an escalation point for complex AV issues and support incident, problem, and change management when needed. Monitor AV infrastructure and performance, identify opportunities for improvement, and test new solutions that make collaboration easier for team members. Deploy and support AI-powered capabilities across meeting rooms and video conferencing, while using AI tooling to improve areas such as monitoring, reporting, documentation, and troubleshooting. Maintain AV asset information, contribute to forecasting and budgeting, and create clear technical documentation and training materials. Build strong relationships with vendors, integrators, and internal partners while identifying better ways of working across the team. Share your knowledge with colleagues, support the onboarding of new team members, and continue developing your own AV expertise.

Who You Are:
You have 3+ years of AV experience and have delivered AV projects through design, integration, commissioning, and ongoing support. You understand the hardware behind sophisticated AV systems, including DSP, control processors, amplifiers, and related technologies, with experience using platforms such as Crestron, Q-SYS, and Dante. Experience configuring Q-SYS designs is a plus, as are certifications such as AVIXA CTS, Q-SYS Level 2, or Dante Level 3. You have hands-on experience deploying, managing, and monitoring video conferencing systems such as Google Meet hardware and Zoom Rooms. You're familiar with fleet management and monitoring tools and can troubleshoot issues across connected AV systems. You have experience supporting senior executives or VIPs and can provide thoughtful, professional, and discreet support when priorities are time-sensitive. You understand IT and networking fundamentals, including how AV systems communicate across enterprise networks. You're familiar with technologies such as Dante and Q-SYS, including multicast, QoS, and clocking, and have experience using ticketing or work-management systems such as Jira. You communicate technical information clearly and create documentation that helps others understand, support, and use AV technology effectively. You’re curious about how AI is changing meetings and collaboration and are comfortable experimenting with AI tools to improve how you work. You enjoy getting to the root cause of technical problems and finding solutions that improve the experience over the long term. You work effectively both independently and with distributed teams, communicate clearly with people across different roles and levels, and build trusted relationships with partners and vendors. You take ownership of your work, adapt thoughtfully to changing priorities, and are motivated to keep learning as AV technology evolves.

Where You'll Be:
This role is based in Stockholm. We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home. We ask that you come in 4-5 times per week.

Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.About the Role As an AV Operations Specialist, you'll be accountable for how the AV spaces perform, how support requests get resolved, and how events land in the space you're responsible for. This role will help own all areas within the AV landscape. In a given week you might execute a preventative maintenance sweep across a floor of conference rooms, work the support queue and drive a recurring failure to root cause, and then run technical coverage for an all-hands or an executive presentation that evening. You'll be the regional presence our AV Engineering and Production teams build on — the person who catches problems before users report them, and who turns what you learn on the ground into standards the rest of the team can run from. Your work directly enables the collaboration and transparency that advance our AI safety mission. Responsibilities Site Ownership & Room Health Serve as the AV owner for your office — accountable for the health, readiness, and performance of every room and event space in the building Execute preventative maintenance programs and recurring room sweeps on a defined cadence, not only in response to tickets Maintain accurate inventory of room systems, peripherals, wireless microphones, cameras, and portable production gear, including spares strategy and replacement cycles Coordinate AV scope for office moves, room reconfigurations, and new-space readiness in partnership with Workplace and AV Engineering Know your estate: maintain the room documentation, as-builts, and site-specific gotchas that make your office supportable by anyone on the team Support Operations Help own the AV support queue — triage, prioritization, resolution, and escalation with clear diagnostic context Participate in the regional AV on-run rotation (West, East, or EMEA), covering AV issues during local business hours alongside the daily room-check discipline Systematically isolate faults to a point in the signal chain rather than reaching for reboots and cable swaps Drive recurring issues to root cause and surface them to AV Engineering as candidates for platform-level or design-level fixes Contribute to runbooks, standard operating procedures, and knowledge base documentation that other company-wide broadcasts Operate event production systems including audio consoles, video switchers, camera systems, playback, and streaming encoders Run pre-event readiness: walkthroughs, rehearsals, source checks, gear staging, and failover planning Handle scoping conversations with requesters — translating what a stakeholder wants the event to feel like into an equipment and staffing plan that fits the team's SLA Turn novel one-off events into repeatable standards — a template, runbook, or gear list that makes the next one easier for the whole team Vendor Direction & Cross-functional Partnership Direct AV integrators, contractors, and event labor on site, holding them to defined scope, SLAs, and quality standards Partner with Workplace, Events, and IT on lead times, expectations, and readiness Act as the regional feedback loop to AV Engineering — what's failing, what's missing, and what the standard should be Communicate status, risk, and resolution to non-technical stakeholders in clear, calm, jargon-free language You May Be a Good Fit If You: Have 8+ years of hands-on experience in AV operations, workplace technology, or technical event support Have owned a standing estate — the same rooms, the same stakeholders, week over week — and were accountable for how those spaces performed over time Bring working fluency across room systems, event audio, video, camera, and streaming, with enough depth to diagnose problems rather than only report them Are comfortable being the only AV person in the building, and can prioritize independently across maintenance, support, and events Bring structure to ambiguity — checklists, intake processes, maintenance cadences, and documentation Are energized rather than drained by being the front-facing technical partner to executives, event producers, and everyone else who walks up to you in a hallway Take ownership end-to-end, from noticing a recurring failure to getting it permanently fixed Thrive in a fast-moving environment where standards are being written rather than inherited Strong Candidates May Also Have Experience With: Q-SYS DSP platforms — comfortable navigating and reasoning about existing audio/video routing and control designs Logitech CollabOS and Sync, Google Meet hardware, Zoom Rooms, and enterprise room system administration Preventative maintenance and room-sweep programs across a distributed room fleet Broadcast video switchers such as Blackmagic ATEM, Ross Carbonite, or NewTek TriCaster Digital audio mixing consoles such as Yamaha DM7 or CL/QL series, and Shure wireless systems PTZ camera systems and multi-camera workflows Ticketing and workflow systems such as Jira, and participation in an on-run rotation Coordinating AV contractors, integrators, and labor for site support and event coverage CTS certification or equivalent demonstrated capability Role Specific Location Policy: This role will be based in our New York office This role is expected to be in office 5 days per week Occasional evening and early-morning coverage is expected around major events 4-6 weeks of travel annually may be expected for this role for distributed support, office And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. rows.title: Betopia Sales Agent — end-to-end ownership
rows.situation: Betopia needed a production AI sales assistant embedded in Odoo CRM, with no existing team or infrastructure for it.
rows.action: Owned the project solo end-to-end — requirement gathering, visiting SBUs and salespeople, collecting won/lost cases and objection-handling knowledge, building the RAG/LLM pipeline, multi-provider routing with failover, the agent itself, backend and admin frontend, CI/CD, deployment, and ongoing production operation.
rows.result: Production system used by 700+ salespersons across Betopia Group.
rows.good_for_tags: ownership, ambiguity, end-to-end execution, working solo

rows.title: Self-onboarding onto an unfamiliar stack
rows.situation: The Sales Agent required Odoo, Redis, Qdrant, and Next.js — none used hands-on before.
rows.action: Learned and integrated all four directly inside a live production build, rather than deferring the project or staying in familiar tools.
rows.result: All four are now core, reliable parts of the production system.
rows.good_for_tags: learning speed, adaptability, comfort with the unfamiliar

rows.education: B.Sc. in Information and Communication Engineering, University of Rajshahi
rows.core_narrative: Niloy builds real AI systems, integrates them with business software, deploys them, and takes responsibility for keeping them working.
rows.primary_identity: AI/ML Engineer focused on production AI systems — Agentic AI, LLM applications, RAG, backend/API engineering, MLOps, applied ML — not someone who only experiments with models.
rows.one_liner: AI/ML Engineer building and deploying scalable AI-powered systems using Python, FastAPI, LLMs, RAG, Agentic AI, and MLOps.
rows.engineering_principle: The model is only one component — a useful AI product needs data, retrieval, state, orchestration, APIs, infrastructure, monitoring, and a reliable user workflow around the model.
rows.avoid_phrases: passionate AI enthusiast, generic claims with no engineering evidence, keyword stuffing, fabricated technologies, inflated metrics, fake leadership claims
rows.working_style: Hands-on, curious, self-directed, comfortable taking ownership, execution-oriented; learns by building and debugging real systems rather than staying theoretical.
rows.leadership_example: Led the Betopia Sales Agent largely solo, covering requirement gathering, visiting SBUs and talking to salespeople, knowledge collection, AI/RAG development, agent development, UI/backend integration, CEO-level updates, salesperson reviews, deployment, CI/CD, monitoring, Odoo integration, and production debugging.
rows.dealbreakers: generic/low-substance roles that don't involve real production systems
rows.reason_for_leaving: Looking for a role with broader ownership and scale, ideally one that also moves my trajectory toward robotics/physical AI.
rows.tone_preferences: Direct, technically precise, no corporate fluff, no excessive motivational language. Concise and credible; avoid exaggerated claims and buzzwords. Every statement must be defensible if asked about in an interview.
